title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Take the 32-bit divider off the EX critical path with an iterative multi-cycle div/rem unit
motivation:
Fmax is 5.44 MHz. The worst path (199.8 ns, 150 logic levels) goes
MEM/WB.rd -> forward_unit -> EX operand mux -> alu -> EX/MEM/dmem. The only
thing in alu.sv that is ~150 LUT levels deep is the combinational
`/` and `%` (signed and unsigned, each a 32-stage ripple
subtract-and-select array). Nearly all of the 12.3k LUT4s are those
dividers too. Everything else in EX (32-bit add/sub, compare, barrel
shift, DSP multiply) takes about 15-25 levels. CoreMark -O3 runs almost
no DIV/REM in its timed loop (list/matrix/state kernels use MUL, add,
shift, compare and branch), so a divide that takes ~34 cycles costs well
under 1% of IPC while it caps the clock of every other instruction.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Take DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU out of the combinational ALU. Put them in a new
sequential radix-2 restoring divider (rtl/div_unit.sv) that sits beside
the ALU in EX, and stall the front of the pipeline while it runs.

div_unit (about 32 iterations plus 1-2 cycles of setup and fixup):
  - IDLE -> BUSY -> DONE FSM. `start` fires when ID/EX holds a valid
    DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU and the unit is IDLE. At start the unit LATCHES the
    post-forwarding operands (rs1/rs2 from the EX forward muxes), the op,
    and the signedness. Latching matters: while the divide is held in EX,
    the instructions ahead of it drain out of EX/MEM and MEM/WB, so the
    forwarding sources that fed its operands disappear.
  - Signed ops take absolute values at start. Each cycle does one
    shift/subtract/select on a 32-bit remainder and a 32-bit quotient. At
    the end it negates the quotient if sign(a)^sign(b) and the remainder
    if sign(a).
  - Special cases are decided at start and go straight to DONE with no
    iterations: divide-by-zero (quotient = all ones, remainder = a) and
    INT_MIN / -1 (quotient = INT_MIN, remainder = 0).
  - DONE holds the result until EX/MEM actually captures it, i.e. until
    the cycle with !stall_ex_mem. A dmem stall that lands in the same
    cycle as completion therefore cannot drop the result. The unit then
    returns to IDLE.
  - Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` the unit keeps the same FSM and
    handshake but runs a short fixed latency (for example 2 cycles) and
    produces the ALTOPS formulas already in alu.sv:
    (a-b)^0x7f8529ec, 0x10e8fd70, 0x8da68fa5, 0x3138d0e1. The stall and
    forwarding path is then still proven by riscv-formal within the
    depth-20 BMC. The real arithmetic is checked by cocotb, cosim and
    formal-deep.

Pipeline integration:
  - div_stall = ID/EX.valid && is_div_op && !div_done. This drives
    stall_if (hold PC) and stall_id (hold ID/EX, no flush). It also makes
    EX/MEM capture a bubble (valid = 0, reg_write = 0, mem_read and
    mem_write = 0, is_illegal = 0) instead of the stalled divide.
    stall_ex_mem (the dmem stall) keeps priority: it holds EX/MEM as it
    does today. A DIV in EX never redirects, so there is no conflict with
    redirect. load_use only fires for a LOAD in ID/EX, so it cannot flush
    a held divide.
  - When the divide completes, EX/MEM.alu_result = div result. The RVFI
    fields EX/MEM.rs1_val and rs2_val come from the divider's latched
    operands, not from the current forward-mux output, which may be stale
    by then.
  - Add a decode-time flag, ctrl.is_div (or alu_op range 15-18), so the
    stall and bubble logic does not decode alu_op in the critical EX path.

Secondary micro-opt in the same file. Replace the three 64-bit products
(mul_ss, mul_uu, mul_su) with ONE signed 33x33 product:
{a[31]&a_signed, a} * {b[31]&b_signed, b}. MUL takes p[31:0] and
MULH/MULHSU/MULHU take p[63:32]. That maps to a single Gowin MULT36X36,
not 6 DSPs, and takes two 32-bit 4:1 result muxes out of the ALU output.
The ALTOPS arms for MUL* stay as they are.

Expected effect. Once the divider is gone, the critical path becomes
forward mux -> DSP multiply, or adder/shifter/compare -> EX/MEM, which is
about 15-25 LUT levels plus one DSP. That should give 35-60 MHz on the
GW2A-18 speed grade (6-11x). CoreMark iterations per cycle drop by less
than 1% (a few hundred divides × ~34 cycles against ~450k cycles per
iteration). LUT4 use should also fall from about 12.3k to about 3-4k.
The projected fitness is therefore several times 12.12. The schema caps
the claim at +50%.

changes.description: New sequential radix-2 restoring divider for DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU with an IDLE/BUSY/DONE FSM. It latches the forwarded operands at start, handles divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 as immediate completion, fixes up signs at the end, and holds the result in DONE until the EX/MEM register advances (!stall_ex_mem). Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS it runs the same FSM with a short fixed latency and emits the ALTOPS (a-b)^K formulas. It also exports its latched operands so RVFI rs1_rdata/rs2_rdata stay correct.

Remove the combinational `/` and `%` arms, and their ALTOPS arms, from the ALU; div/rem results now come from div_unit. Replace mul_ss/mul_uu/mul_su with one signed 33x33 multiply (operand sign bits chosen by op) and pick the low or high 32 bits. Keep the MUL* ALTOPS arms unchanged.

Instantiate div_unit and feed it the post-forward rs1/rs2. Add a div_stall output. On div_stall (and no dmem stall), EX/MEM captures a bubble (valid=0, reg_write/mem_read/mem_write=0). On div_done, EX/MEM takes alu_result = div result and rs1_val/rs2_val = the divider's latched operands. Pass the stall_ex_mem input to the divider as its "consume" gate.
Add a div_stall input. OR it into stall_if and stall_id, and do not assert flush_id for it. The dmem-stall rule that EX/MEM holds is unchanged and takes precedence.
Route div_stall from ex_stage to hazard_unit. No change to top-level IO.
Add ctrl_t.is_div so stall detection does not have to compare the 5-bit alu_op in EX.
Set is_div=1 for funct7=0000001 and funct3 in {4,5,6,7}. is_illegal discipline is unchanged.

Remove the DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU vectors from the combinational ALU test (they move to test_div_unit.py). Keep and extend the MUL/MULH/MULHSU/ MULHU vectors, including INT_MIN, -1, 0 and 0xFFFFFFFF operand mixes, to exercise the merged 33x33 multiplier.

New clocked cocotb test for div_unit. Carry over the full div/rem vector set (30+ per op, including divide by zero, INT_MIN/-1, negative operands and random values checked against Python reference semantics). Also test the handshake: result held while the consume gate (stall) is asserted, and back-to-back divides.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r1s0 (improvement, +788.61%): The combinational `/` and `%` in alu.sv (a 32-stage ripple subtract array, ~150 LUT levels, most of the 12.3k LUT4s) capped Fmax at 5.44 MHz for every instruction, so moving DIV/REM into an iterative div_unit that stalls the front end and latches its post-forwarding operands (the forwarding sources drain during the stall) paid off hugely at almost no CoreMark IPC cost, because the timed loop runs almost no divides.

title: Move MUL/DIV out of the 1-cycle EX ALU into a multi-cycle muldiv unit that stalls EX
motivation:
The core runs at 5.442 MHz. The worst path (199.8 ns, 156 cells) is
clock -> u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_ex/u_alu -> u_ex: forwarding mux -> the fully
combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` (two 32-stage array dividers, signed and
unsigned) plus three separate 64-bit multipliers (mul_ss, mul_uu, mul_su)
-> EX/MEM register. Everything else in this 5-stage pipeline (32-bit add,
branch compare, forwarding, hazard logic, LUT-RAM dmem read) is on the
order of 15-30 ns. The single-cycle divider is ~7-10x longer than any
other path, so Fmax is capped purely by an operation that CoreMark almost
never executes inside the timed region (the timed kernels -- list,
matrix, state machine, CRC -- are MUL-heavy in matrix_* but essentially
DIV-free). The divider/multiplier array is also most of the 12.3k LUT4.
Fitness = iter/cycle x Fmax, and here one term is off by an order of
magnitude; paying a few percent of IPC for it is overwhelmingly favourable.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure EX so the ALU is single-cycle only for RV32I ops, and route all
eight M-extension ops to a new sequential `muldiv` unit with a
start/busy/done handshake that stalls the pipeline at EX:

1. New rtl/muldiv.sv.
   * On `start` (M-op in ID/EX, unit idle, not already completed for this
     instruction) latch the POST-FORWARD rs1/rs2 values and the op into
     internal registers. All iteration logic works from these registers
     only, so the forwarding muxes are never in series with the arithmetic.
   * Multiply: ONE 33x33 signed multiplier (a_ext = {a[31]&a_signed, a},
     b_ext = {b[31]&b_signed, b}) replaces the three 64-bit multipliers;
     MUL takes lo, MULH/MULHU/MULHSU take hi. Operands come from the
     latched registers, so the path is reg -> DSP (MULT18X18 x4 / MULT36X36)
     -> hi/lo mux -> EX/MEM reg. `done` asserts the cycle after start
     (1 stall cycle per MUL).
   * Divide: radix-2 restoring/non-restoring divider on |a| and |b|,
     one quotient bit per cycle (~33-34 cycles incl. setup/sign-fixup).
     Per-cycle path is a 33-bit subtract + mux, far shorter than anything
     else in the core. RV32M special cases: divisor==0 -> quotient
     0xFFFFFFFF, remainder = dividend (skip sign fixup); INT_MIN / -1 falls
     out naturally (quotient 0x80000000, remainder 0) but keep an explicit
     check for clarity. Optionally early-out divisor==0 in 1 cycle.
   * The result register is held (done stays high) until the pipeline
     actually advances the M-op into EX/MEM, so a concurrent dmem stall
     (EX/MEM frozen) cannot drop the result.
   * `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS`: compute the exact same ALTOPS stand-in
     formulas currently in alu.sv from the latched operands, with the
     1-cycle MUL latency for ALL eight ops (no 33-cycle divide under
     formal) so BMC depth and the liveness check are unaffected while
     still exercising the stall/handshake/forwarding path. This matters:
     formal/checks_si.cfg runs liveness at depth 20 ("liveness 1 10 20"),
     so a 33-cycle divide under ALTOPS would stall past the window.
2. rtl/alu.sv: delete the M-ext cases, the `*`, `/`, `%` operators and the
   64-bit product signals. Keep RV32I ops only (ALTOPS ifdef moves to
   muldiv.sv).
3. rtl/ex_stage.sv: instantiate muldiv; add `is_muldiv` detection
   (alu_op in ALU_MUL..ALU_REMU, or a new ctrl bit from the decoder).
   While an M-op is in ID/EX and !done: EX/MEM captures a bubble
   (valid=0, reg_write=0, mem_read/mem_write=0) and a `muldiv_busy`
   output is raised. On done: EX/MEM captures the M-op with
   alu_result = muldiv result and rs1_val/rs2_val = the latched operands
   (RVFI correctness -- the forwarding sources may have drained by then).
4. rtl/hazard_unit.sv: new input muldiv_busy -> stall_if and stall_id
   (hold PC and ID/EX, NOT flush_id). dmem_stall keeps priority over
   everything as today; redirect cannot coincide with an M-op in EX.
   Load-use detection is unchanged (the M-op in ID/EX is never a load).
5. rtl/decoder.sv / core_pkg.sv: optionally add ctrl.is_muldiv decoded in
   ID so EX doesn't need a 5-bit range compare on alu_op in its stall
   path. is_illegal discipline unchanged.
6. rtl/core.sv: wire muldiv_busy from EX to the hazard unit.

Expected result: the critical path moves to the RV32I EX loop
(fwd mux -> 32-bit add/compare -> redirect -> PC / NOP-mux -> load-use ->
stall) or the dmem LUT-RAM read, both in the ~20-30 ns range, i.e.
Fmax ~35-50 MHz (6-9x). IPC cost: +1 cycle per MUL (matrix kernels) and
~33 per DIV (near zero in the timed region), estimated 2-5% CPI increase.
LUT4 should also drop substantially (two array dividers + two redundant
64-bit multipliers removed). Net fitness gain far exceeds +50% (the
schema cap).

title: Zero-bubble fetch-stage prediction: IF predecode + 64x2b bimodal BHT + always-taken JAL
motivation:
Every taken branch and JAL currently costs one fetch slot: control
transfers resolve in EX and the instruction fetched in that cycle
(pc+4) is flushed (flush_if/flush_id on `redirect`). Measured with the
reference ISS on the exact eval binary (CoreMark 2K, -O3, 10 iters,
between the start/stop markers):
  2,922,015 instructions retired, 4,491,485 cycles (CPI 1.54)
  529,588 conditional branches, 294,425 taken
  49,367 JAL, 13,735 JALR (all of them returns)
  => 357,527 taken transfers = 12.2% of instructions = ~8% of cycles.
The penalty is not hidden by the 22% imem stall model: the stall bit is
an independent per-cycle sequence, so fetching the target one cycle
later shifts the whole fetch stream by one cycle.
Fmax (~5.4 MHz) is pinned by the 150-level combinational divider path
(u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_alu -> EX/MEM/dmem). A fetch-side predictor is
entirely off that path (in the timed harness imem data comes from an
LFSR flop; the new path is flop -> predecode/BHT read -> 32b add -> PC,
~20-30 levels vs 150), so saved cycles convert ~1:1 into fitness.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
imem is zero-wait, so the fetched word is available combinationally in
IF in the same cycle its PC is presented. Predecode it in IF and steer
next_pc speculatively, so correctly predicted transfers cost 0 cycles:
  * JAL (opcode 1101111): predicted taken, target = pc + J-imm (exact).
  * BRANCH (opcode 1100011, funct3 not 2/3): direction = MSB of a
    64-entry x 2-bit bimodal BHT indexed by pc[7:2] (flop array,
    reset to 2'b01 weakly-not-taken, combinational read in IF);
    target = pc + B-imm (exact). The BHT is trained from EX with the
    resolved outcome of every valid branch (saturating +/-1 at the EX
    instruction's pc[7:2]), gated by !stall_ex_mem so a branch held
    during a dmem stall updates exactly once.
  * Never predict when target bit[1] is set (B-imm bit1 = instr[9],
    J-imm bit1 = instr[22]); the misaligned-target trap path stays
    exactly as today (no redirect, pc_next = pc+4).
  * JALR is not predicted (redirects as today). All CoreMark JALRs are
    returns (13.7k = 0.3% of cycles). A RAS was evaluated and left out
    because it would need a 32-bit pred_target in ID/EX and an EX
    comparator for that 0.3%.
PC steering: pc <= reset ? 0 : redirect ? redirect_target :
!stall ? (pred_taken ? pc+imm_pred : pc+4) : pc. pred_taken is forced 0
whenever the IF payload is flushed (redirect / imem stall), and a held
(load-use / dmem-stall) fetch recomputes it next cycle. A single
1-bit `pred_taken` rides IF/ID -> ID/EX (cleared on flush like
everything else); no target needs to be carried because EX recomputes
pc+imm with the same value.
EX redirect becomes a misprediction check (robust to arbitrary
instruction streams, e.g. predicted-taken words that decode illegal):
  real_xfer = (branch_taken || is_jump) && !misalign_fault   (old redirect)
  redirect  = pred_taken ? !(real_xfer && !is_jalr) : real_xfer
  redirect_target = (pred_taken && !real_xfer) ? pc+4
                  : is_jump ? jump_target : branch_target
pc_next, trap and every RVFI field are computed from the true outcome
exactly as now, so only architecturally-correct instructions retire.
The redirect shadow is still exactly the one instruction in IF,
so wrong-path handling is unchanged.
Expected cycles, from replaying the same trace through this predictor
model: taken-transfer bubbles 357.5k -> 51.8k branch mispredictions
(8.4% of branches) + 13.7k JALR = 65.6k, i.e. ~292k cycles saved
(-6.5% cycles). Fmax unchanged, so fitness goes from 12.12 to about
12.95 (+7%).

changes.description: Add 1-bit `pred_taken` to if_id_t and id_ex_t.

New module. Combinational predecode of the fetched word (BRANCH with valid funct3 / JAL, B- and J-immediates, target bit[1] check), a 64x2-bit bimodal BHT in flops with synchronous reset to 2'b01, read at fetch pc[7:2] and written from an EX update port (en, pc[7:2], taken) with saturating counters. Outputs pred_taken and pred_target = pc + imm.

Instantiate branch_predictor. next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target : (pred_taken ? pred_target : pc + 4); PC priority unchanged (reset > redirect > !stall). out.pred_taken = pred_taken && !(flush || redirect). Add the BHT update input ports and pass them through.
Latch in.pred_taken into ID/EX (zeroed on reset/flush, held on stall).

Replace redirect/redirect_target with the misprediction form above (real_xfer vs pred_taken, fall-through target pc+4). Export BHT update signals: bht_upd_en = in.valid && in.ctrl.is_branch, bht_upd_pc = in.pc, bht_upd_taken = branch_taken. pc_next, trap and EX/MEM contents are unchanged.
Wire EX's BHT update port to IF, gating the enable with !stall_ex_mem. Otherwise the top level is unchanged. IO and RVFI are unchanged.

Add directed tests: a backward counted loop (BHT trains, result correct), a forward branch that is mispredicted and later learned, JAL/call-return correctness, a misaligned branch/JAL target that still traps with no redirect, a predicted-taken word with branch opcode and funct3=2 (illegal) that must fall through to pc+4, and a mispredict that lands in the same cycle as an imem stall or a dmem stall. Update any existing assertion that hard-codes the old taken-branch bubble timing.
Add 1-bit `pred_taken` to if_id_t and id_ex_t.

New module. Combinational predecode of the fetched word (BRANCH with valid funct3 / JAL, B- and J-immediates, target bit[1] check), a 64x2-bit bimodal BHT in flops with synchronous reset to 2'b01, read at fetch pc[7:2] and written from an EX update port (en, pc[7:2], taken) with saturating counters. Outputs pred_taken and pred_target = pc + imm.

Instantiate branch_predictor. next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target : (pred_taken ? pred_target : pc + 4); PC priority unchanged (reset > redirect > !stall). out.pred_taken = pred_taken && !(flush || redirect). Add the BHT update input ports and pass them through.
Latch in.pred_taken into ID/EX (zeroed on reset/flush, held on stall).

Replace redirect/redirect_target with the misprediction form above (real_xfer vs pred_taken, fall-through target pc+4). Export BHT update signals: bht_upd_en = in.valid && in.ctrl.is_branch, bht_upd_pc = in.pc, bht_upd_taken = branch_taken. pc_next, trap and EX/MEM contents are unchanged.
Wire EX's BHT update port to IF, gating the enable with !stall_ex_mem. Otherwise the top level is unchanged. IO and RVFI are unchanged.

Add directed tests: a backward counted loop (BHT trains, result correct), a forward branch that is mispredicted and later learned, JAL/call-return correctness, a misaligned branch/JAL target that still traps with no redirect, a predicted-taken word with branch opcode and funct3=2 (illegal) that must fall through to pc+4, and a mispredict that lands in the same cycle as an imem stall or a dmem stall. lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r1s2 (regression, +9.65%): Predicting taken branches and JALs in IF (predecode, a 64x2b bimodal BHT trained from EX, and a 1-bit pred_taken carried to EX for the mispredict check) is a real IPC win that beat its ~7% trace-replay estimate, and it counts as a regression only because it was built on the old 5.4 MHz divider-bound base instead of hyp-001's 107.7 core, so port it there, but on that 48 MHz, 15-level core the imem->predecode->BHT->32-bit pc+imm adder->next_pc path (~20-30 levels) would likely become the new critical path, so precompute or pipeline the predicted target rather than adding it in the same cycle.

title: Shorten the EX critical paths: registered one-hot forwarding selects, dedicated AGU, redirect decoupled from IF/decode
motivation:
I ran `make timing` on the champion (hyp-001, 47.9-48.4 MHz). It shows
two paths tied at ~26.15 ns:
(1) path 1, 15 cells: regfile sync-read RAM DO (Gowin absorbed ID/EX
rs_val as the RAM output register) -> write-first/hold LUT -> 3-LUT
forward mux on rs2 -> alu_b mux -> mul sign-ext LUT -> DSP MULT
(B[35]->DOUT[37]) -> 6-LUT ALU-op/div-OR/jump-link output mux -> dmem
address hold mux -> BSRAM ADB. The EX/MEM alu_result flop is absorbed
into the dmem BSRAM address register, so the multiplier and the whole
result mux feed the BSRAM address.
(2) path 4, 44 cells: RAM DO -> forward mux -> 32-bit compare carry
chain -> 6-LUT redirect logic -> IF NOP-substitution mux ->
regfile read-address (rs1_addr_w) -> hazard load-use ->
ID/EX stall/flush -> rs1_val RESET.
Fixing only one path leaves the other at 26 ns, so both must be cut
together. The muxes on these paths mostly serve rare cases: the NOP
substitution, the jump-link mux, the div OR, the ALU-op decode on 5
encoded bits, and the live forward compares.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Four coordinated micro-optimizations, all keeping the 5-stage shape and
CoreMark cycle count (it may drop slightly):

1. Registered forwarding selects. Compute forwarding in ID, not EX.
   Compare the IF/ID instruction's rs1/rs2 (raw imem_data[19:15] /
   [24:20]) against (a) ID/EX.rd with ID/EX.ctrl.reg_write (distance 1,
   which will sit in EX/MEM next cycle) and (b) EX/MEM.rd with
   EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write && !mem_misalign (distance 2, which will sit in
   MEM/WB next cycle). Priority is dist1 > dist2 > regfile, with rd != 0.
   Latch one-hot selects into ID/EX:
   {sel_exmem, sel_wb_alu, sel_wb_load, sel_rf} per operand. For
   distance 2, EX/MEM.ctrl.mem_to_reg picks between the MEM/WB
   alu_result and read_data sources.
   This is exact because ID/EX captures only when !stall_id, and
   stall_id covers every case where EX/MEM or MEM/WB would not advance
   (dmem_stall). On dmem_stall all forwarding sources freeze, and the
   MEM/WB data fields are already retained. div_unit already latches its
   operands in its first EX cycle.
   EX's forward mux becomes a 4-source AND-OR on flop-driven selects
   (EX/MEM.alu_result, MEM/WB.alu_result, MEM/WB.read_data,
   ID/EX.rs?_val). That removes the compare levels and the wb_stage
   mem_to_reg mux from every EX path: ALU, branch compare, JALR target
   and store data. forward_unit.sv is deleted or reduced. The regfile
   write-first bypass still covers distance 3.
   Post-trap reg_write corner cases: a misaligned load is caught by
   gating dist2 with mem_stage's combinational mem_misalign. For
   control flow, every JAL/JALR/taken branch now redirects, even when
   misaligned. On a misaligned-target trap, the redirect target is
   pc+4, which pc_next already reports. The instruction behind is
   flushed and re-fetched, so it is decoded again against EX/MEM with
   the trapped reg_write=0. This also simplifies redirect to
   (branch_taken || is_jump).

2. Dedicated AGU. Add a separate adder mem_addr = rs1_fwd + imm in EX,
   registered as a new EX/MEM.mem_addr field. It drives io_dmemAddr,
   byte masks, misalign checks, load alignment and RVFI mem_addr in
   mem_stage. The BSRAM address path becomes 4:1 forward mux -> adder
   -> BSRAM, instead of going through alu_a/alu_b muxes, the ALU-op
   case mux, the div OR and the jump mux. alu_result keeps
   feeding forwarding and WB.

3. Take redirect out of IF/decode/hazard. if_stage passes raw imem_data
   to ID with no NOP substitution. ID/EX captures a '0 bubble through
   flush_id = (load_use || redirect || (imem_stall && !div_stall)) &&
   !dmem_stall. The '0 bubble matches the old NOP for every consumer:
   rd=0, valid=0, no mem op. The hazard unit's load-use compare now
   reads the raw imem_data fields. This is equivalent, because a
   redirecting instruction in EX is never a LOAD, so load-use cannot
   fire alongside redirect. After this change redirect reaches only
   the PC mux and the ID/EX flush.

4. Flatter ALU output and MUL operands. Decode a one-hot result-class
   select in ID and register it into ID/EX. The classes are add/sub,
   logic, slt, shift, lui, mul_lo, mul_hi, link(pc+4) and div. EX
   combines them with a flat AND-OR, so the div OR and the is_jump
   link mux merge into that one OR level. The link value pc+4 is
   precomputed in ID. The multiplier takes its operands straight from
   the forwarded rs1/rs2, not alu_a/alu_b, with mul_a_signed and
   mul_b_signed as registered ID/EX bits. Keep the ALTOPS branch
   consistent.

5. Stall only on source registers that are really used (cheap IPC win).
   Qualify the load-use compare with uses_rs1 =
   !(instr[2] && (instr[4] || instr[3])), which excludes
   LUI/AUIPC/JAL, and uses_rs2 = instr[5] && !instr[2]
   (OP/STORE/BRANCH). This removes spurious load-use bubbles when an
   I-type immediate happens to alias the load's rd.

Expected: the BSRAM address no longer depends on the MUL/ALU (the AGU
path is ~4 LUT + short carry). The MUL->alu_result flop path drops
from 13 to ~9 cells. The redirect path loses the IF mux, regfile
address and hazard segment, leaving compare -> redirect -> ID/EX flush.
Fmax goes from 48.4 MHz to ~56-60 MHz. The next limit is likely DSP ->
result mux -> EX/MEM, or compare -> ID/EX flush fanout. IPC stays flat or rises slightly.
Area cost is ~32 LUT + ~40 FF for the AGU and the select flops, less
the removed forward_unit and NOP mux.

title: Re-cut the ID/EX boundary: regfile read + bypass + forward-select done in ID so EX starts from real flops, plus a dedicated AGU driving dmem
motivation:
The champion (hyp-001, 48.4 MHz) is limited by a 26.2 ns / 15-cell path
that STARTS inside the register file (cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s0, a Gowin
BSRAM instance: bsram=6 = 4 for the bench dmem + 2 for the two regfile read
ports) and ENDS at the dmem BSRAM address register (dmem_1_dmem_1_0_0_s).
Gowin maps the regfile to synchronous-read block RAM by absorbing the ID/EX
rs1_val/rs2_val flops into the BSRAM address register, so architecturally
the regfile read is actually performed in the EX cycle: BSRAM clock-to-out
(slow) -> u_id stall/flush/x0/write-first bypass muxes -> forward_unit rd
comparators -> forwarding mux -> AUIPC/imm operand mux -> ALU add -> 11-way
ALU result mux -> "| div_result" -> is_jump pc+4 mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result,
which is itself absorbed into the dmem BSRAM address register (BSRAM setup).
Two slow BSRAM timing arcs plus ~6 levels of muxing wrap a single 32-bit
add. The second-worst path (seen as critical in hyp-002 at 27.5 ns) is the
same forwarding front end feeding the branch comparator -> redirect ->
if_stage NOP mux -> hazard load-use compare -> ID/EX enable fan-out.
Both are pipeline-cut problems, not arithmetic problems.

Measured probe (make timing, place_option 0, champion RTL + only
`(* syn_ramstyle = "registers" *)` on reg_file.regs): BSRAM 6 -> 4
(confirms the regfile was in BSRAM), Fmax 48.06 MHz (unchanged alone),
and ALL top-5 paths now start at MEM/WB.rd -> u_fwd comparators:
  - 26.10 ns, 52 cells: u_fwd > u_ex (branch cmp/redirect) > u_if (NOP
    mux) > u_hazard > u_id > u_if pc   (redirect-into-decode chain)
  - 26.09 ns, 17 cells: u_fwd > u_ex > u_alu > u_ex -> dmem BSRAM
  - 26.07 ns, 49 cells: u_fwd > u_ex > u_if > u_rf -> ID/EX rs1/rs2_val
So items 2 (registered forward selects), 3 (AGU) and 4 (redirect out of
the decode cone) each remove a stage of every current top path; item 1
is neutral alone but stops the BSRAM clock-to-out re-becoming the start
point once the comparators are gone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move work out of EX into ID so the EX stage begins at plain flip-flops,
and give the dmem address its own short path:

1. Register file becomes a true ID-stage combinational read. Mark the
   `regs` array with Gowin/Synplify attributes that forbid block-RAM
   inference (`(* syn_ramstyle = "registers" *)`, falling back to
   "distributed_ram" if LUT count or timing is better) so no ID/EX flop is
   absorbed into a BSRAM. The read (x0 check + WB write-first bypass) now
   completes in ID from the fetched word (imem data is a register in the
   timed bench) and lands in real ID/EX rs1_val/rs2_val flops. ~1k FFs +
   ~600 LUT4 for the read muxes; well within the 10k LUT budget.

2. Forwarding selects precomputed in ID and registered in ID/EX. In ID,
   compare if_id rs1/rs2 against the instruction entering EX/MEM next
   cycle (ID/EX.rd & reg_write & valid) and against the one entering
   MEM/WB (EX/MEM.rd & reg_write). Store one-hot fwd_exmem/fwd_memwb bits
   in ID/EX. All stall cases are consistent with this: on dmem_stall
   ID/EX, EX/MEM and MEM/WB data all hold; on div_stall the divider has
   already latched its operands on its first EX cycle; on load-use / imem
   stall / redirect ID/EX captures a bubble and the selects are recomputed
   when the consumer re-enters. The EX-side forward_unit comparators
   disappear from both the ALU path and the branch/redirect path. Keep the
   MEM/WB-hold behaviour (data retained, valid cleared) unchanged.

3. Dedicated AGU. Add a separate EX adder `rs1_fwd + imm` whose result is
   registered in a new EX/MEM `mem_addr` field that alone drives
   io_dmemAddr, byte-mask/misalign logic and the load-extract shift. The
   dmem-address path is then flop -> 2:1 forward mux -> 32-bit carry chain
   -> BSRAM address, skipping the ALU result mux, the div OR and the jump
   mux. alu_result keeps feeding forwarding/WB as before.

4. Take `redirect` out of the ID decode cone: if_stage no longer forces
   the fetched word to NOP on redirect (flush_id already zeroes ID/EX that
   cycle and the PC load has priority over stall), and hazard_unit's
   load-use compare uses the raw fetched rs1/rs2. This removes the
   redirect -> NOP mux -> decoder/regfile/hazard -> ID/EX chain (keep the
   NOP on imem_stall only, or gate only `valid`).

Expected result: the EX critical path drops from ~15 cells with two BSRAM
arcs to ~8-9 cells starting at a flop, and the branch path loses the
comparators and the redirect-into-decode fan-out. The next limiter should
be the flop -> forward mux -> 33x33 DSP multiply -> result mux path or the
branch compare -> PC path, both estimated at ~15-16 ns. Estimate 48 ->
~60-65 MHz with IPC unchanged (no new bubbles; the pipeline depth and
hazard rules are identical).

title: Port the IF bimodal-BHT + JAL predictor to the 48 MHz core, keeping EX redirect shallow
motivation:
The champion (hyp-001, 107.70, Fmax 48.4 MHz, 4,491,817 cycles) still
resolves every control transfer in EX and flushes the pc+4 fetch, so every
taken branch / JAL / JALR costs one fetch slot: 357.5k taken transfers in
the timed CoreMark window (294k taken branches, 49k JAL, 13.7k JALR), about
8% of all cycles. The 22% imem stall bits are an independent per-cycle
sequence, so the bubble is not hidden by stalls.
hyp-003-r1s2 already built exactly this predictor (IF predecode, 64x2b
bimodal BHT, JAL always taken, 1-bit pred_taken to EX) on the old
divider-bound base and measured the IPC win in the real eval: cycles
4,491,485 -> 4,201,766 (-6.45%, IPC +6.9%), formal and cosim passed. It
"regressed" only because it was not built on hyp-001. The champion's cycle
count is essentially the baseline's (4,491,817), so the same ~290k-cycle
saving is available. LESSONS warns that on the 48 MHz core the new logic
must not lengthen critical paths: the champion is limited at 26.2 ns by the
EX forward-mux -> ALU -> dmem-address path, and hyp-002 showed the EX
redirect path (fwd -> branch compare -> if NOP mux -> hazard -> ID/EX
flush) sitting at 27.5 ns right behind it. So the port has to keep the
mispredict check no deeper than today's `redirect`, and ideally shallower.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add zero-bubble fetch prediction and restructure the EX redirect so the
deep branch-compare output goes through at most one extra LUT.

IF (same cycle as ID; imem data in the timed harness comes straight from
an LFSR flop, so this path starts at a flop):
  * Predecode the fetched word: BRANCH (opcode 1100011, funct3 not 2/3)
    and JAL (1101111). JALR is not predicted.
  * Direction: MSB of a 64 x 2-bit bimodal BHT in flops indexed by
    pc[7:2] (reset 2'b01), JAL always taken. Never predict when target
    bit1 is set (B-imm bit1 = instr[9], J-imm bit1 = instr[22]), so the
    misaligned-target trap path is unchanged.
  * pred_target = pc + (JAL ? J-imm : B-imm), one 32-bit carry chain.
    PC priority stays reset > redirect > !stall; next_pc = pred_taken ?
    pred_target : pc+4. The path is LFSR/pc flop -> 2 predecode levels
    + 64:1 mux (MUX2_LUT5..8) -> carry chain -> 2 muxes -> pc, roughly
    12-15 ns, well under the 26 ns EX path.
  * pred_taken is forced to 0 whenever the IF payload is invalid (imem
    stall or redirect); a held fetch (load-use/dmem/div stall) simply
    recomputes it next cycle.

ID (precompute everything EX needs except the compare itself), latched
into ID/EX next to a 1-bit pred_taken:
  * alt_target = pred_taken ? pc+4 : pc+imm (the IF adder output is
    reused: IF and ID are the same cycle), i.e. the place to go if the
    prediction proves wrong for a branch / unpredicted JAL.
  * br_q = valid & is_branch, br_mis_q = imm[1] (branch-target
    misalignment is known at decode because pc[1:0] = 0),
    force_redir_q = valid & JAL & !pred_taken (only reachable from
    arbitrary formal instruction streams), jalr_q = valid & is_jalr.

EX mispredict check (replaces `redirect`):
  redirect = (br_q & (cond ? !pred_q & !br_mis_q : pred_q))
           | force_redir_q
           | (jalr_q & !jalr_misalign)
  redirect_target = jalr_q ? {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0} : alt_target_q
`cond` (forward mux -> 32-bit compare -> funct3 select) feeds one LUT
with registered side inputs instead of today's taken/jump/misalign
(branch_target[1:0] from the EX pc+imm adder) combination, and the
redirect_target mux loses its pc+imm adder input. pc_next, trap,
reg_write and all RVFI fields are still computed in EX from the true
outcome exactly as now, so only architecturally correct instructions
retire and the redirect shadow is still exactly the one IF instruction.

Two further timing guards so the predictor does not become the critical
path:
  * BHT training is registered: EX writes {en, pc[7:2], taken, ctr} to a
    small flop stage (en = br_q & !stall_ex_mem, so a branch held in a
    dmem stall trains once) and the counter array is updated the next
    cycle from the 2-bit counter value that was read in IF and carried
    down ID/EX (no second 64:1 read port, and `cond` drives only a
    flop, not 128 counter D-inputs). One-cycle-late / slightly stale
    training costs negligible accuracy.
  * Drop `redirect` from if_stage's NOP-substitution mux (out.instr /
    out.valid use only the imem-stall flush): on a redirect cycle the
    PC takes redirect_target and flush_id zeroes ID/EX regardless of
    what load-use says, so the NOP only lengthened redirect -> rs1/rs2
    -> hazard compare -> stall/flush fanout (the hyp-002 critical path).
    ID/EX's flush still kills the wrong-path instruction.

Expected: cycles 4.49M -> ~4.20M (the measured r1s2 result: taken
bubbles 357k -> ~52k branch mispredicts + 13.7k JALR), IPC +6.9%.
Fmax should hold at ~48 MHz because the EX ALU->dmem path is untouched
and the EX redirect path is no deeper (likely shallower), giving about
107.7 * 1.069 = ~115 (+6-7%).

title: Flatten EX's two tied critical cones: registered WB data, flop-selected MUL result, precomputed redirect, control-only ID/EX flush
motivation:
Measured on the champion RTL (hyp-20260930-002-r2s1) with
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench`, place_option 0: 66.85 MHz, two tied
critical cones, both starting at the high-fanout MEM/WB flop
cpu/u_mem/reg_q.ctrl.mem_to_reg (data delay budget = period):

Path 1, 14.925 ns -> cpu/u_ex/reg_q.alu_result_0 (D):
  c2q 0.23
  u_wb wb_w_data mux (mem_to_reg ? read_data : alu_result)  1.29
  u_ex rs2 forward mux (2 LUTs)                              1.69
  u_ex alu_b mux (alu_src|is_jump ? alu_imm : rs2)           1.26
  u_alu n16 (b[31] & mul_b_signed, 33rd operand bit)         1.06
  DSP mul_p (B[35] -> DOUT)                                  4.38
  ALU result mux + "| div_result": 5 LUT levels              5.01
Path 2, 14.665 ns -> RESET pin of every u_id/reg_q.* flop (paths 2..25):
  c2q + u_wb mux + forward mux (2 LUTs)                      ~3.1
  branch comparator carry chain                              ~3.2
  n889_s6 / n889_s4 (branch_op cond mux)                     ~1.8
  u_if n69_s63 / n69_s5 (misalign + redirect, fanout 33)     ~2.7
  u_id n129 = reset|flush_id, fanout 192 -> RESET net         2.4

Every one of those extra muxes has a select that is known one stage
earlier: mem_to_reg and both data inputs exist in MEM; is_mul/is_mulh,
alu_src/is_jump, branch_op and the static misalign bit (imm[1]) are all
known in ID. And the 192-way flush fanout exists only because the whole
ID/EX payload, not just its control bits, is synchronously cleared on a
bubble. So both cones can lose 3-5 LUT levels with no change to pipeline
depth, hazard rules or IPC.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming micro-optimisations, in priority order. The first four together
cut both tied paths; the fifth adds margin on path 1. IPC stays
bit-identical (cosim cycle count 4,491,817 unchanged), so fitness scales
with Fmax alone.

A. Registered WB data (both paths, about -1.2 ns). mem_stage computes
   wb_data = ctrl.mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result and registers it in
   a new mem_wb_t.wb_data field. wb_stage drives regfile w_data from that
   flop, ex_stage's MEM/WB forward source is that flop, and RVFI
   rd_wdata reads it. The extra LUT goes on the MEM-side path
   dmem BSRAM rdata -> shift/sext -> MEM/WB flop, which ends at a flop and
   has slack. Fold it into the load-extract case where possible. hold_wb
   semantics are unchanged: every data field, including wb_data, is
   retained and only valid is cleared.

B. Flop-selected MUL result (path 1, about -2.5 ns). Register is_mul and
   mul_hi in ID/EX (from the decoder) and restructure alu.sv so the
   output is
     out = mul_q ? (mulhi_q ? p[63:32] : p[31:0]) : nonmul
   where nonmul is the existing case over the other ops plus the
   div_result OR (div_result is a flop, zero unless DONE). The DSP output
   is then one LUT5 (LUT4 + MUX2_LUT5) from the EX/MEM flop instead of
   five levels, and the non-MUL tree runs in parallel with the 4.4 ns DSP.
   Also register mul_a_signed/mul_b_signed in ID/EX. The
   RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS arms keep the same substitutes, in the same mul
   slot.

C. Precomputed redirect (path 2, about -1.5 ns). Hardwire if_stage
   pc[1:0] = 2'b00. This is architecturally exact: reset is 0, pc+4
   keeps alignment, and a redirect only fires when the target is aligned,
   because a misaligned target is trapped and suppressed. After that,
   branch_target[1:0] = imm[1:0] and JAL's target[1:0] = imm[1:0]. In ID,
   register one-hot branch-condition selects already gated with
   "is_branch && !imm[1]" (sel_eq, sel_ne, sel_lt, sel_ge, sel_ltu,
   sel_geu), plus jal_ok = is_jal && !imm[1], plus is_jalr. EX then
   computes
     redirect = |(sel & {eq,!eq,lt,!lt,ltu,!ltu}) | jal_ok
                | (is_jalr & !agu_sum[1])
   in about 2 LUT levels after the comparators, instead of 4. The
   misalign trap bits for RVFI/ctrl use the same precomputed terms,
   for example misalign_branch = is_branch && cond && imm_q[1]. pc_next
   and redirect_target are unchanged in value.

D. Control-only ID/EX flush (path 2, about -0.8 ns). Split the ID/EX
   always_ff. Only valid, reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_branch,
   is_jump/is_jalr, is_div, is_illegal and the new redirect/branch
   selects take `reset || flush`. All datapath fields (pc, rs1_val,
   rs2_val, imm, alu_imm, instr, rd, rs?_addr, fwd bits, alu_op,
   mem_width, ...) use only `if (!stall) capture`. A bubble with those
   control bits cleared has no architectural effect (hazard load-use
   needs mem_read, ID forwarding needs reg_write, div start needs
   valid && is_div, RVFI needs valid, and redirect/misalign need
   is_branch/is_jump). On load-use flush (stall=1) the data just holds.
   This cuts the redirect -> flush fanout from 192 to about 20 loads.

E. ID-side ALU operand pre-select (path 1, about -1.2 ns; do it if
   timing shows path 1 is back on top). Register opa_val =
   (is_auipc|is_jump) ? pc : rs1_data and opb_val = (alu_src|is_jump) ?
   alu_imm : rs2_data, with their own forward bits (fwd1_* & !use_pc,
   fwd2_* & !use_imm). The ALU inputs then come from a flop-sourced 3:1
   forward mux with no pc/imm mux behind it. The existing rs1/rs2
   forward muxes stay for the AGU, branch compare, JALR, store data,
   div_unit and RVFI.

Estimate: path 1 goes from 14.9 to about 10-11 ns and path 2 from 14.7
to about 11 ns. The next limiters should be forward -> AGU -> dmem BSRAM
address and forward -> JALR target -> PC, both around 10-11 ns.
Expected Fmax 67-68.5 -> ~80-85 MHz. Budget-conservative claim: +15%.
Cost: about 100 extra FFs and a handful of LUTs, with 3183 LUT4 and
1666 FF today.

mem_write, is_branch, is_jump, is_jalr, is_div, is_illegal and the
selects) are cleared by reset||flush, and the datapath fields only
obey !stall.

(is_jalr & !agu_sum[1]). misalign_branch/jump come from the

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r3s0 (improvement, +30.17%): After r2s1's forwarding/AGU/regfile cuts, both tied ~14.9 ns cones at 66.85 MHz were chains of muxes whose selects were already known one stage earlier, so moving each select back a stage doubled the +15% estimate (198.60, about 87 MHz inferred, with IPC bit-identical at 4,491,817 cycles); the moves were WB's mem_to_reg mux into a registered MEM/WB wb_data that also serves as the forward source, the MUL hi/lo/signedness decode into ID/EX flops so the DSP output meets one LUT5 while the non-MUL tree runs in parallel, pc/imm ALU operands pre-selected in ID, and one-hot branch-condition selects gated with the static misalign bit imm[1] (the PC is kept word-aligned with pc[1:0] hardwired to 0); the other cut cleared only the ID/EX control bits on flush, because a synchronous clear of the whole payload became a 192-fanout RESET net at the end of the redirect path, so check every LUT level on a critical path for a select that could be registered and keep flushes control-only.

title: Re-cut the EX loop: distance-2 bypass moved into ID (EX forward = one LUT4), MUL enters the result mux last, ID/EX flush clears control bits only
motivation:
Measured on the champion RTL (make timing TARGET=bench, place_option 0,
66.8 MHz): all 25 worst setup paths start at MEM/WB.ctrl.mem_to_reg and
split into two nearly tied families (period 5 ns constraint; data delay
14.93 ns vs 14.67 ns):

Path 1 (12 levels, -> EX/MEM.alu_result[0]):
  mem_to_reg (fanout 32) -> u_wb wb_w_data mux (fanout 35)
  -> EX forward mux, 2 LUT levels (rs2_31_s5, rs2_31_s4; 7 inputs/bit:
     fwd_ex & ex_mem.we ? EX/MEM : fwd_wb & mem_wb.we ? wb_data : rs_val)
  -> alu_b operand mux -> 33rd-bit sign-extend LUT -> DSP MULT (3.78 ns)
  -> FIVE LUT levels of ALU result mux / "| div_result" -> flop.
  Arrival 5.56 -> 8.54 ns is spent in WB mux + bypass alone (~3 ns);
  another ~4.5 ns is the result-mux tree after the DSP.

Path 2 (13 levels, -> ID/EX RESET, 24 of the 25 paths):
  same mem_to_reg -> WB mux -> 2-level bypass (-> 8.43 ns)
  -> 1.8 ns route -> 32-bit branch compare carry chain
  -> 2 LUTs branch_cond/misalign -> 2 LUTs in u_if (redirect/PC select,
     fanout 33) -> u_id "reset || flush" LUT, fanout 192, 1.45 ns route
  -> synchronous RESET pin of every ID/EX flop (pc, instr, rs vals ...).

So the shared prefix (WB mux + 2-level bypass, ~3 ns) is the first thing
to cut, and each family then has its own ~1-3 ns of avoidable tail.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Three coordinated cuts, judged together (lesson from r2s1: tied paths
must be cut together or the probe reads flat).

1. Distance-2 bypass moves from EX into ID (the structural change).
   When an instruction is captured into ID/EX, its distance-2 producer is
   in the MEM stage and its final value is already available there
   combinationally: EX/MEM.alu_result (ALU/JAL/JALR link/DIV result) or
   the aligned load_data (ID/EX only captures when !dmem_stall, so a
   load in MEM has valid data). MEM computes
     mem_result = ctrl.mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result
     mem_fwd_we = ctrl_with_trap.reg_write   (misaligned load clears it)
   and ID captures
     rs?_val <= (rs? != 0 && mem_fwd_we && ex_mem.rd == rs?) ? mem_result
                                                           : rs?_data
   with the MEM forward as the LAST 2:1 level before the ID/EX flop (the
   regfile read keeps its x0 check and WB write-first bypass, now used
   for distance 3). MEM/WB carries the pre-muxed wb_data, so the WB mux
   disappears (regfile write data, write-first bypass, RVFI rd_wdata all
   read MEM/WB.wb_data). EX keeps only the distance-1 bypass:
     rs? = (fwd?_ex && ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write) ? ex_mem.alu_result : rs?_val
   = 4 flop-driven inputs = one LUT4 per bit. fwd?_wb, the MEM/WB forward
   ports and the mem_to_reg fanout into EX are deleted. IPC is unchanged:
   this delivers exactly the value the old MEM/WB->EX forward delivered
   one cycle later; load-use is still one bubble (after the bubble the
   load sits in MEM while its consumer is in ID), a load at distance 2
   still costs nothing. Safe by the invariant id_stage already documents:
   whenever ID/EX captures a real instruction EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance
   too (dmem stall freezes all three, load-use bubbles ID/EX, a held DIV*
   latches its operands), so a value captured into ID/EX never goes stale.

2. MUL joins the result mux at the final level. Feed the DSP straight
   from the forwarded rs1/rs2 (MUL* are R-type, so the alu_a/alu_b
   operand mux is not needed on that path) with the 33rd sign bit folded
   into the bypass LUT (rs[31] & signed flag from ID/EX). Decode in ID and
   register in ID/EX one-hot result selects: sel_mul_lo, sel_mul_hi, and
   a one-hot (or small-group) select for the remaining ALU results; build
   out = (sel_mul_lo & p[31:0]) | (sel_mul_hi & p[63:32]) |
         rest_result | div_result
   where rest_result (adder/logic/shift/SLT/LUI, all faster than the
   DSP's 3.78 ns) is AND-OR muxed in parallel. The DSP output then sees
   ~1 LUT level instead of 5.

3. ID/EX flush clears only what a bubble needs. Replace "reset || flush
   -> '0 on all ~190 ID/EX flops" with: on flush clear valid and the
   control bits that have side effects or feed hazard/forward logic
   (reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_branch, is_jump, is_jalr, is_div,
   is_illegal, fwd?_ex); leave pc/instr/imm/rs?_val/rd/alu_op data flops
   untouched (valid=0 makes them don't-care; reset still clears all).
   This drops the redirect->flush net from fanout 192 to ~12 and takes
   ~1-1.4 ns off path 2. Optionally precompute branch_target and its
   misalignment in ID (pc + imm are both known there) so the EX redirect
   only needs compare-result & registered flags.

Expected: path 1 loses ~3 LUT levels + the mem_to_reg/wb fanout nets
(~5-6 ns), path 2 loses the same bypass prefix plus the 192-fanout
reset net (~3.5-4 ns). The next limiter should be the branch compare ->
redirect -> PC path or the AGU -> dmem address path at ~11-12 ns, i.e.
roughly 80-88 MHz vs 66.8-68.5 MHz, at identical cycles/iteration. The
new ID path (dmem read data -> byte align/sext -> mem_to_reg mux -> ID
bypass -> ID/EX) is ~5 LUT levels and was far from critical before
(the existing dmem -> MEM/WB.read_data path is not in the top 25).
Area roughly neutral (64 bypass LUTs move from EX to ID; WB mux and
fwd_wb LUTs removed).

title: Stack the IF bimodal-BHT + JAL predictor on the 68.5 MHz champion with a timing-safe carry-select target and mispredict-only EX redirect
motivation:
The champion (r2s1, 152.57, 68.53 MHz, 4,491,817 cycles) still resolves
every control transfer in EX. IF and ID share one cycle (no IF/ID flop),
so each taken branch / JAL / JALR costs one fetch slot: ~357k taken
transfers in the timed window (294k taken branches, 49k JAL, 13.7k
JALR), ~8% of all cycles. r1s2 and r2s2 measured the IF predictor
(predecode + 64x2b bimodal BHT + JAL always taken) at 4.49M -> 4.20M
cycles (IPC +6.9%) with formal and cosim passing, and on the 48 MHz core
it held Fmax. It was never stacked on r2s1 (LESSONS r2s2). The open risk
is timing: at r2s1's ~14.6 ns period the r2s2 IF path (imem word ->
predecode -> BHT select -> 32-bit pc+imm adder -> next_pc) may no longer
have slack, so this port shortens that path by construction instead of
hoping. r2s1's critical path (MEM/WB mem_to_reg -> WB mux -> forward mux
-> ALU -> EX/MEM alu_result, 12 levels) is not touched.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep r2s1 exactly as is (forwarding selects in ID, AGU, flop regfile,
ALU link pc+4) and add a zero-bubble fetch predictor:

IF (imem data in the timed harness is an LFSR flop, the PC is a flop):
  * Predecode the raw imem word (not the NOP-muxed one): BRANCH (opcode
    1100011, funct3 != 2,3) and JAL (1101111). JALR is not predicted.
  * Direction: bimodal BHT of 2-bit counters indexed by the PC *flop*
    (pc[10:2], 512 entries, Gowin distributed RAM via
    (* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *); if it lands in flops instead
    use 256 entries pc[9:2]), so the table read runs in parallel with
    the imem access and is off the imem-data cone. JAL is always taken.
    ISS trace of the timed CoreMark window (2.92M insns, 529.6k
    branches, 294.4k taken, 49.4k JAL, 13.7k JALR): bimodal mispredicts
    are 51.8k @64 entries (matches r1s2's measured cycle saving),
    44.3k @256, 39.8k @512, 39.6k @1024; gshare-1k only reaches 38.0k,
    so 512-entry bimodal is the size/accuracy knee. A RAS would catch
    all 13.7k returns but saves only ~0.3% of cycles and puts a 32-bit
    target compare in EX, so it is left out.
    Never predict when the target is misaligned: imm[1] = instr[8]
    (B-type) / instr[21] (J-type); pc[1:0] is always 00, so this keeps
    the misaligned-target trap path identical.
    pred_taken = imem_ready & !imm1 & (is_jal | (is_br & ctr[1])).
  * Target, carry-select so the imem-data -> PC path is a ~19-bit carry
    chain plus two muxes: lo = pc[20:2] + imm[20:2] (B-imm sign-extended
    to 21 bits) gives the carry c; hi = select(pc[31:21],
    pc[31:21]+1, pc[31:21]-1) by {imm[20], c}, where the +1/-1 are
    computed from the PC flop in parallel with the fetch. (If timing
    shows plenty of slack, a plain 32-bit adder is acceptable.)
  * next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target : pred_taken ? pred_target :
    pc+4; PC priority unchanged (reset > redirect > !stall). Whenever
    the PC advances, ID/EX captures the same instruction and its
    prediction, so held fetches just recompute the prediction.
  * Keep redirect out of the IF NOP mux (already the case in r2s1).

ID: register into ID/EX a 1-bit pred_taken, the BHT counter snapshot,
br_q = valid & is_branch, br_mis_q = B-imm[1], jalr_q, and
alt_target = pred_taken ? pc+4 : pred_target (the IF adder output is
reused because IF and ID are the same cycle): the only place a branch /
JAL can need to go if the prediction proves wrong.

EX: replace redirect with the mispredict form
  redirect = (br_q & (cond ? (!pred_q & !br_mis_q) : pred_q))
           | (jal_q & !pred_q & !jal_mis_q)      // formal-only corner
           | (jalr_q & !jalr_misalign)
  redirect_target = jalr_q ? {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0} : alt_target_q
so the deep `cond` (forward mux -> compare -> funct3 select) meets only
registered side inputs, and the EX pc+imm adder leaves the redirect
target path (it stays only on the pc_next/RVFI side, which is pruned).
pc_next, trap, reg_write and every EX/MEM field keep coming from the
true outcome exactly as now, so only architecturally correct
instructions retire; the redirect shadow is still the single IF
instruction, and the dmem-stall behaviour (redirect reloads the PC while
ID/EX holds) is unchanged.

BHT training is registered: EX writes {en = br_q & !stall_ex_mem,
idx, taken = cond, ctr_snapshot} into one flop stage and the saturating
update lands in the table the following cycle (single read port, cond
drives one flop instead of 512 counter D-inputs). The BHT may be a
reset-less async-read array (Gowin distributed RAM, 1W1R) because any
table content is architecturally safe: EX verifies every prediction.
Keep a deterministic init (initial block to 2'b01 or sync reset if it
stays in flops) so cosim cycle counts are reproducible.

Expected: cycles 4.49M -> ~4.18M (taken-transfer bubbles 357k ->
~40k branch mispredicts + 13.7k JALR), IPC +7.3%, Fmax held at ~67-69 MHz
because no new logic sits on the r2s1 critical path and the EX redirect
cone gets shallower: ~152.6 * 1.07 = ~163.

title: Fold the live reg_write forward qualification into ID-registered one-hot selects and flatten the EX redirect cone
motivation:
The champion r3s0 (198.60, 89.2 MHz, 4,491,817 cycles) is limited by a
16.36 ns, 33-cell path from cpu/u_mem/reg_q.ctrl.reg_write (MEM/WB) through
EX to cpu/u_if/pc_q. The path starts on MEM/WB.ctrl.reg_write because EX
still qualifies every forward select with the live EX/MEM and MEM/WB
reg_write flops (`in.fwd1_wb && fwd_mem_wb_w_en`). That flop fans out
to 128 forward-mux bits (rs1, rs2, alu_a, alu_b), the regfile write enable
and the regfile write-first bypass compares, so the path pays a high-fanout
net plus a qualification LUT level before the operand mux, then the
comparator / JALR AGU carry chain, the 8-term redirect AND-OR and the PC
mux. The r2s1 WB->forward->ALU->EX/MEM path (seed 0 at 90.4 MHz, 12 cells)
starts on the same qualification. LESSONS r3s0 says to look at every LUT level
on a critical path for a select that could be registered one stage earlier.
This qualification is one of those selects.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Everything the live reg_write qualification tells EX is already known when
the consumer is captured into ID/EX. Whenever ID/EX captures a real
instruction, EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance in the same cycle (dmem stall, DIV and
load-use all hold or bubble ID/EX). So the value EX would read from those
flops is exactly the value being written into them on that edge:
  * MEM/WB.reg_write(next) = mem_stage.ctrl_with_trap.reg_write
    = EX/MEM.reg_write && !mem_misalign. This is shallow logic on EX/MEM
    flops.
  * EX/MEM.reg_write(next) = ID/EX.reg_write && !misalign_jump. For JAL,
    misalign_jump is the static imm[1]. For JALR it is agu_sum[1], a 2-bit
    carry off the forwarded rs1[1:0], so it is a short path.
Export these two "reg_write_next" bits from mem_stage/ex_stage into
id_stage. Compute fully qualified, priority-resolved, one-hot forward
selects there:
  sel_ex = ex_rw_next && rd match
  sel_wb = wb_rw_next && rd match && !sel_ex
Register them per consumer (rs1, rs2, alu_a, alu_b), masked by use_pc /
use_imm for alu_a / alu_b as now. Also zero the ID/EX opa/opb/rs?_val
payload when a forward is selected. Each EX operand then becomes a plain
AND-OR on flops, (ex & sel_ex) | (wb & sel_wb) | val_q. That is one LUT5
instead of two or three LUT levels, and EX no longer reads
fwd_ex_mem_w_en / fwd_mem_wb_w_en, so the start of both critical cones
moves from a fanout-130 net to low-fanout ID/EX select flops (one per
operand, duplicated if needed).
Two small cuts in the same redirect cone are stacked on this:
  (1) Merge lt/ltu into one 33-bit borrow compare. A registered cmp_unsigned
      bit drives the extended sign bit. ID registers 4 one-hot selects
      (eq, ne, lt, ge) plus jal_ok. The redirect is then
      (s_eq&eq)|(s_ne&!eq)|(s_lt&lt)|(s_ge&!lt)|jal_ok|(is_jalr&!agu1),
      which is one fewer comparator input and one fewer LUT level, and it
      removes one 32-bit carry chain.
  (2) Precompute the branch/JAL target pc+imm in ID into a registered
      target_q. B/J imm is selected by instr[3], so there is no imm_gen
      dependence. EX's redirect_target is then
      is_jalr ? {agu_sum[31:1],0} : target_q, and the EX pc+imm adder is
      removed from the PC mux inputs (pc_next for RVFI can reuse target_q).
IPC is bit-identical (same forwarding, same redirects, same cycle count
4,491,817). Expected Fmax gain is 1-2 LUT levels plus one high-fanout net
(~1.0-1.5 ns of the ~11.2 ns period), giving about 97-102 MHz, i.e.
+8-14% fitness.
Correctness notes for the implementer:
  - The id_stage comment's invariant (matches stay valid while the
    instruction waits in ID/EX) must hold for the qualification too.
    dmem stall freezes all three registers, so it holds. A held DIV
    latches its operands on its first EX cycle, and later bubbles do not
    matter because the DIV result does not depend on the forward muxes.
  - rs1_val/rs2_val sent to RVFI must still be the post-forward values.
    Take them from the EX muxes, never from the zeroed payload.
  - The regfile write enable and bypass keep using MEM/WB reg_write.
    Only the EX forward path loses it.

title: Decoupled front end: 2-entry fetch queue between IF and ID hides imem stalls behind back-end stalls
motivation:
The champion (hyp-20260930-001-r3s0: 198.60, 89.2 MHz, 4,491,817 cycles)
couples fetch to decode. stall_if = load_use | imem_stall | dmem_stall |
div_stall, so the PC holds on every cycle the back end is frozen (a dmem
stall on a LOAD/STORE in EX/MEM, a load-use bubble, a 35-cycle divide) and
the imem slot, which is ready 78% of the time, is thrown away and fetched
again later. On top of that, every cycle imem is not ready (22%, one
independent xorshift draw per cycle in both cosim and bench_stall_gen.sv,
whether or not a fetch is requested) sends a bubble into ID even when the
back end could accept an instruction. In CoreMark the back end stalls on
roughly 0.14 cycles per instruction (loads and stores are about 1/3 of
the mix at a 0.28-cycle expected dstall each, plus load-use) and imem
stalls cost about 0.28 cycles per instruction. The two are independent,
so a small buffer that keeps fetching while the back end is frozen turns
a good share of the later istall cycles into instructions already
waiting in ID. None of this touches the EX redirect, forward or ALU cones
that set Fmax.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Put a 2-entry instruction queue (each entry holds pc[31:2] and a 32-bit
instr; registered count 0..2) between the PC and ID. The front end then
runs ahead of the back end by up to two instructions.

Fetch side (if_stage):
  fetch_fire = imem_ready && (count_q != 2) && !redirect
  The PC advances on fetch_fire (pc_q + 1) and loads redirect_target on
  redirect; as today, redirect has priority. Because fetch_fire depends
  only on the registered count and the flop-driven imem_ready, the PC
  enable no longer reads load-use, dmem_stall or div_stall. With
  count_q == 2 fetch pauses for one cycle, but the queue still feeds ID,
  so throughput is unaffected.
Decode side:
  head = (count_q == 0) ? {pc, imem_data} : entry0
  head_valid = (count_q != 0) || imem_ready
  Empty-bypass keeps today's zero-latency path. The select is a
  registered flag, so the only cost is one flop-selected LUT level on
  the imem -> decoder / regfile-address path, which starts at the imem
  LFSR flop and is not near-critical. ID consumes the head when ID/EX
  captures, i.e. deq = head_valid && !stall_id. The IF/ID bundle
  becomes {head.pc, head_valid ? head.instr : NOP, head_valid}, so
  decoder, imm_gen, the regfile read addresses, the ID forward matches
  and the load-use comparator all read the head exactly where they now
  read the IF/ID bundle.
Enqueue: the fetched word is written at index count_q - deq unless it is
bypassed straight into ID (count_q == 0 && deq). If deq, entry1 shifts
into entry0.
Redirect: count_q <= 0 (clears only the queue control state; the entry
data is plain datapath, following the control-only flush lesson). ID/EX
is still bubbled through flush_id. The word fetched in the redirect cycle
is dropped, as it is today.
Hazard unit: stall_if becomes "queue cannot accept" (only count_q == 2),
flush_if becomes !head_valid, and stall_id / flush_id / stall_ex_mem /
hold_mem_wb keep their current definitions. The back end (ID/EX,
EX/MEM, MEM/WB, forwarding, div, RVFI order) is untouched, so the
invariants the ID forward matches rely on still hold.

Expected: about 5-7% fewer cycles (0.08-0.11 hidden istall cycles per
instruction at CPI ~1.6), with Fmax unchanged within noise because every
new signal on the PC enable, queue count and head select is a flop or
one LUT from flops.

from the hazard/ID side. Clear count_q on redirect or reset. Output
the head as the if_id_t bundle, with valid = head_valid and instr
forced to NOP when the head is not valid.

Decouple the PC hold from the back-end stalls. The IF side only
needs the queue state (stall_if drops load_use, dmem_stall and
div_stall), flush_if = !head_valid, and ID dequeue = !stall_id.
stall_id, flush_id, stall_ex_mem and hold_mem_wb are unchanged.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r4s1 (regression, +3.34%): A 2-entry fetch queue between IF and ID (the PC keeps fetching while load-use, dmem stalls or a divide freeze the back end, and an empty queue bypasses the fetched word straight into ID) gave a real but small gain, 205.23 against 198.60, about half its 5-7% cycle estimate and under the 4.6% acceptance bar (cycles and Fmax were not recorded, so the split between them is unknown); the likely reason is that the queue fills only during back-end stall cycles (~0.14 per instruction) and every EX redirect clears it, so few banked instructions survive to cover a later imem stall, while the estimate counted almost every back-end stall cycle as a hidden istall; discount such estimates for CoreMark's taken-branch rate, and because the gain is orthogonal to r4s0's Fmax cuts but too small to clear the bar alone, bundle the queue with the IF predictor, whose fewer redirects should also keep the queue full longer.

title: Stack a 512-entry bimodal-BHT + always-taken-JAL IF predictor on r3s0, with a mispredict-only redirect folded into the existing one-hot selects (no extra EX->PC depth)
motivation:
The champion (r3s0, 198.60, 89.2 MHz median, 4,491,817 cycles) still
resolves every control transfer in EX. IF and ID share one cycle, so
each taken branch / JAL / JALR costs one fetch bubble: about 357k
taken transfers in the timed window (294k taken branches, 49k JAL,
13.7k JALR), ~8% of all cycles. The IF predictor has been measured
three times (r1s2, r2s2, r3s2), always with formal and cosim passing.
r3s2 on r2s1 went from 4,491,817 to 4,188,685 cycles (+7.2% IPC) and
lost only ~1-2% Fmax. LESSONS r3s2 says to re-stack it on r3s0 and
merge its mispredict-only redirect with r3s0's precomputed redirect.

I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (place_option 0,
90.37 MHz). There are three cones tied within 0.05 ns, all at ~10.8 ns
of data delay:
  (a) MEM/WB.reg_write -> rs1 forward mux (2 LUT) -> comparator carry
      chain -> u_if n69 redirect AND-OR (4 LUTs, fanout 32) -> pc_q CE
      (fanout 30). The same cone also ends at u_id/valid_q RESET via
      flush_id.
  (b) MEM/WB.reg_write -> alu_b forward mux -> mul_b_signed&b[31]
      -> DSP (3.78 ns) -> 2 LUTs -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
  (c) stall_gen/imem_ready (fanout 1069!) -> if_stage NOP mux on the
      instruction word (rs2_addr_w, fanout 70, 4.4 ns route) -> regfile
      read mux -> rs2_data -> ID/EX opb_val.
Because the tie is three-way, pipelining any one of them (for example
a registered redirect) buys no Fmax. The predictor is the one lever in
this category that pays: it is an IPC gain. The design rule for it is
to add no LUT level to cone (a) and no load to cone (c).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep all of r3s0 unchanged and add a zero-bubble fetch predictor.

1. IF (if_stage.sv). The imem word is an LFSR flop in the timed
   harness, and the PC is a flop.
   * Predecode the raw imem word: BRANCH (opcode 1100011, funct3 not
     2/3) and JAL (1101111). JALR is not predicted (13.7k, 0.3% of
     cycles, not worth a 32-bit target compare in EX).
   * Direction: 512 x 2-bit bimodal BHT indexed by pc_q[10:2], the PC
     flop, so the read runs in parallel with the fetch. Map it to
     Gowin distributed RAM (* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *),
     which gave lutram=32 in r3s2; fall back to 256 entries if needed.
     Initialise to weakly-not-taken. In an ISS trace of the timed
     window, bimodal mispredicts are 39.8k @512 vs 51.8k @64, and
     gshare-1k only reaches 38.0k.
   * pred_taken = !imm1 & (is_jal | (is_br & ctr[1])), with
     imm1 = instr[8] (B) / instr[21] (J). It is NOT gated by
     imem_ready: when imem stalls, stall_if already holds the PC, and
     ID/EX's pred bit is a control flop cleared for bubbles. Misaligned
     targets are never predicted, so the misalign trap path is
     unchanged (not predicted, EX traps it, no redirect).
   * Target: carry-select. lo = pc[20:2] + imm[20:2] (B or J imm, one
     LUT select on the bits that differ) gives carry c. hi is
     pc[31:21], pc[31:21]+1 or pc[31:21]-1, selected by {imm sign, c},
     with the +/-1 values computed from the PC flop in parallel with
     the fetch. The r3s2 structure is kept.
   * PC: CE is unchanged (reset | redirect | !stall_if). D becomes
     redirect ? redirect_target : (pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+1).
     redirect stays the LAST mux level, so cone (a) is not deepened.
     Estimated IF cone: LFSR -> predecode / LUTRAM read -> pred ->
     2 muxes, about 7-8 ns (under the 10.8 ns tie).
   * BHT write port from flops: EX training is registered one cycle
     late (we_q, idx_q, new_ctr_q, from the 2-bit ctr snapshot carried
     down the pipe). Train only on valid branches when EX/MEM advances.

2. Keep cone (c) flat (if_stage.sv, id_stage.sv). Remove the
   imem_ready NOP mux from the instruction bits. ID decodes the raw
   imem word, and instead imem_ready (in.valid) is ANDed into the ~17
   ID/EX control flops (valid, reg_write, mem_read, mem_write,
   is_branch, is_jump, is_jalr, is_div, is_illegal, sel_*, pred). This
   is the same control-only-clear idea r3s0 used for the redirect flush.
   A bubble's data fields are don't-care. A spurious load-use compare
   against the garbage word during an imem stall is harmless: the PC
   is already held, and ID/EX gets a bubble either way. This takes
   imem_ready off the regfile address / decoder / imm_gen fanout
   (1069 today) and gives the new IF predictor logic room.

3. ID (id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv). The IF adder is reused, because IF
   and ID share the cycle. alt_target = pred_taken ? pc+4 : pred_target
   is registered into ID/EX; it is the only place a branch can need to
   go on a mispredict. Fold the prediction into r3s0's six one-hot
   selects so EX's redirect keeps the exact same shape:
     s_eq  = (BEQ  & !pred) | (BNE  & pred)   s_ne  = (BNE  & !pred) | (BEQ  & pred)
     s_lt  = (BLT  & !pred) | (BGE  & pred)   s_ge  = (BGE  & !pred) | (BLT  & pred)
     s_ltu = (BLTU & !pred) | (BGEU & pred)   s_geu = (BGEU & !pred) | (BLTU & pred)
   Each is still gated by br_ok (valid branch, !imm[1]). An aligned JAL
   is always predicted, so jal_ok drops out of the redirect entirely.

4. EX (ex_stage.sv).
     redirect = s_eq&eq | s_ne&!eq | s_lt&lt | s_ge&!lt | s_ltu&ltu
              | s_geu&!ltu | (jalr & !agu_sum[1])
   This is the same AND-OR depth as today, minus the jal_ok term.
     redirect_target = is_jalr ? {agu_sum[31:1],0} : alt_target_q
   alt_target_q is a flop, so the EX pc+imm adder leaves the PC path.
   pc_next, trap, reg_write and every EX/MEM / RVFI field keep their
   current computation (RVFI-only logic is pruned). Wrong-path handling,
   flush_id = (load_use | redirect) & !dmem_stall, and the redirect-
   over-stall PC priority are all unchanged.

at 4,188,685), +7.2% IPC. Fmax should hold at ~88-90 MHz: cone (a)
gains no level, cone (b) is untouched, and cone (c) loses the 1069-way
imem_ready fanout. Fitness is about 198.6 x 1.072 x (0.98..1.0), so
+5% to +7%.

title: Flatten the four tied ~16.2 ns cones: registered one-hot forward/ALU/branch selects + flat opcode-bit operand select
motivation:
I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion r4s2 (232.78; 97.5 MHz
median; placement option 0 gives 91.55 MHz, 7-10 levels). Four
independent cones end within 0.17 ns of each other (period ~10.9 ns),
so no single cut helps. All of them have LUT levels whose selects could
be registered or flattened:
 P1 -5.923 opa_val_31 -> alu_result_7 (the DSP path). Two forward-mux
    LUTs (alu_a_31_s71/s72, fanout 35), then n4_s3 (the 33rd operand
    bit a[31] & mul_a_signed) in series before the DSP A input, the
    DSP itself (3.76 ns), then 2 LUTs (mul_hi mux, mul_sel mux).
 P2 -5.895 MEM/WB.wb_data_7 -> pc_q (33 cells). Two forward-mux LUTs
    (rs2_7_s1/s2), the 25-cell compare carry chain, 4 LUT levels of the
    7-term redirect AND-OR (redirect_Z_s11/s4/s0/s, fanout 34), then the
    PC CE LUT (fanout 30). The same cone ends at the ID/EX control flops
    through flush_id (-5.788).
 P3 -5.891 fwda_wb -> alu_result_13 (10 levels). fwda_wb (fanout 32,
    1.4 ns route) feeds 2 forward-mux LUTs (the second at fanout 11 with
    a 2.1 ns route), 2 shifter LUTs, then 4 LUTs of the 5-bit
    case(alu_op) result mux plus the mul_sel mux.
 P4 -5.754 imem word (lfsr_28) -> data_q.opb_val_0 (9 levels). The
    instruction bits go through 5 LUTs of shared decoder logic
    (n282_s8, dec_alu_op_0_s4, dec_alu_op_2_s2, n282_s6, n282_s2) just
    to form use_imm, then the opb pre-select (fanout 35) and the
    regfile read bypass (rs2_data_w_0_s1, fanout 31, 2.2 ns route).
Cutting only one or two cones buys at most ~0.17 ns. r4s0 proved
registered qualified forward selects are worth ~0.8 ns on its base and
are orthogonal to r4s2's predictor. It has never been stacked on r4s2.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Pure timing cuts. IPC is bit-identical (4,188,685 cycles). Each cut hits
one or more of the tied cones:
A (P1, P2, P3). Port r4s0's registered forward selects. Export
  ex_rw_next = ID/EX.reg_write && !misalign_jump from ex_stage and
  wb_rw_next = EX/MEM.reg_write && !mem_misalign from mem_stage. Whenever
  ID/EX captures a real instruction, EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance on the
  same edge, so these are the values EX would see. In ID, register
  priority-resolved one-hot selects per consumer (rs1, rs2, alu_a,
  alu_b; alu_a/alu_b masked by use_pc/use_imm):
  sel_ex = ex_rw_next && match_ex,
  sel_wb = wb_rw_next && match_wb && !sel_ex.
  Zero the rs?_val/opa/opb payload flop when a forward is selected. Each
  EX operand is then the flop-driven (ex & sel_ex) | (wb & sel_wb) | val_q
  in one LUT (LUT5), and EX no longer reads the live fanout-130 reg_write
  flops. Duplicate each select flop per 16-bit half so no select drives
  32+ loads.
B (P1). The DSP's 33rd operand bits. Register sign-gated copies of the
  selects, sel_ex_sa = sel_ex & mul_a_signed (and so on for wb, and for
  the payload bit opa_val[31] & mul_a_signed; same for b). The
  extension bit becomes its own flop-driven AND-OR in parallel with bit
  31, which takes n4_s3 off the DSP input path.
C (P3, P1 tail). One-hot ALU result select. ID registers group selects:
  add/sub (one adder with a registered invert bit), logic (2 registered
  bits pick AND/OR/XOR in a single LUT per bit), shift (registered
  left/right and arith bits), slt (taken from the one adder's 33-bit
  borrow, with a registered unsigned bit), lui, mul_lo, mul_hi. The
  non-MUL result is an AND-OR of the group outputs, with div_in ORed in.
  The DSP output meets a single 5-input function,
  (mul_lo_q & p_lo) | (mul_hi_q & p_hi) | nonmul (a LUT5 with MUX2_LUT5),
  in place of two chained muxes. The ALTOPS branch is unchanged.
D (P2, flush_id). Merge cmp_lt/cmp_ltu into one 33-bit borrow compare.
  The extension bit is rs?[31] & !cmp_unsigned_q, with the select
  registered in ID. The redirect becomes 4 prediction-folded selects,
  (s_eq&eq)|(s_ne&!eq)|(s_lt&lt)|(s_ge&!lt)|(is_jalr&!agu_sum[1]),
  written as LUT4(s_eq, s_ne, eq, LUT4(s_lt, s_ge, lt, jalr_ok)). That
  is 2 levels after the carry chains instead of 4, and it drops one
  32-bit compare chain (lt and ltu from the same subtract).
E (P4). Flat operand-select decode in id_stage, straight from opcode
  bits, with no sharing with decoder alu_op/alu_src logic:
  use_imm = !(instr[5] & instr[4] & !instr[2]) (only OP needs rs2;
  BRANCH/STORE/LOAD/FENCE/SYSTEM ALU results are don't-care),
  use_pc = instr[2] & !(instr[5] & instr[4]) (JAL, JALR, AUIPC; FENCE
  is don't-care), is_jump_f = instr[6] & instr[2] & !instr[4] for the
  alu_imm=4 select. Each is one LUT3 from the imem word. The decoder
  outputs for RVFI, trap and ctrl are unchanged. Use these same bits for
  the fwda/fwdb masking.
Estimate: P1 -1.0 ns (A+B), P2 -1.4 ns (A+D), P3 -1.2 ns (A+C),
P4 -2 ns (E). The binding cone should then fall from ~10.9 to ~9.8 ns
on option 0 (91.5 -> ~102 MHz), and to ~107 MHz on the median, about
+10% fitness. It is not larger because unseen cones (IF predictor
target, dmem/BSRAM) may surface at ~9.5-10 ns.
Correctness notes for the implementer:
- RVFI rs1_rdata/rs2_rdata must stay the post-forward values. Take them
  from the EX AND-OR muxes, never from the zeroed payload. Keep the DIV
  latched-operand override.
- The regfile write enable and bypass keep using MEM/WB reg_write.
- A dmem stall freezes all three registers and a held DIV latches its
  operands on its first EX cycle, so the registered selects stay valid
  for as long as the instruction waits in ID/EX.
- E's don't-care cases must never feed an architectural result. The
  only ALU users are OP, OP-IMM, LUI, AUIPC, JAL/JALR (link) and MUL.
  Branch compares use rs1/rs2 (the fwd1/fwd2 path) and loads/stores
  use the AGU.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r5s0 (regression, +3.93%): Stacking five select-flattening cuts on r4s2's four tied ~10.9 ns cones scored 241.93 against 232.78, or about 101.3 MHz and ~0.39 ns saved (inferred, assuming cycles stayed at 4,188,685; no post-change timing report), which is under 40% of the ~1 ns estimate and less than half of the ~0.8 ns that r4s0's registered forward selects alone saved on their older base; the cuts were those selects, sign-gated DSP extension bits, a one-hot group-select ALU AND-OR with one 33-bit adder serving add/sub/slt, a single borrow compare with a 2-level redirect, and opcode-bit LUT3 use_imm/use_pc; the likely cause, unconfirmed but flagged by the hypothesis itself, is that at a ~10 ns period the top-4 paths of one place_option report hide a dense next tier of untouched cones (IF predictor target, dmem BSRAM, the fixed 3.76 ns DSP), so the next-worst untouched cone sets the gain rather than the depth of the cut; before estimating, list many distinct endpoints, bundle Fmax-only gains this small with an orthogonal IPC win such as r4s1's fetch queue to clear the 4.6% bar, and keep a flat post-DSP OR tree under `(* syn_keep = 1 *)` or synthesis re-associates it and puts OR levels after the DSP output.

title: Decoupled front end on the predictor core: 4-entry pointer-based fetch queue (flop-only write enables) between IF and ID
motivation:
The champion (hyp-20260930-003-r4s2: 232.78, 97.5 MHz, 4,188,685 cycles)
still couples fetch to decode: stall_if = load_use | !imem_ready |
dmem_stall | div_stall. Every cycle the back end is frozen (dmem stall
on a LOAD/STORE in MEM, a load-use bubble, a 35-cycle divide) the imem
slot, ready 78% of the time, is thrown away, and every later cycle
imem is not ready (22%, an independent draw per cycle whether or not a
fetch is requested) sends a bubble into ID even though the back end
could have taken an instruction. The imem port is 32 bits wide, so
fetch bandwidth (0.78 instr/cycle) is the real bottleneck of this
core; the only way to recover it is to bank instructions during the
back-end stall cycles and spend them on later imem stalls.

hyp-20260930-002-r4s1 built exactly this on r3s0 (no predictor) and
measured 4,491,817 -> 4,348,100 cycles (-3.2%) with Fmax unchanged
(89.2 MHz), about half its estimate. Its LESSONS entry names the
reason: every EX redirect clears the queue, and without a predictor
every taken branch and JAL redirected (~10% of all instructions), so
most banked instructions were thrown away before they covered an
istall. On r4s2, predicted-taken branches and JALs redirect in IF
with no bubble and EX redirects only on a mispredict or JALR (the
predictor alone removed ~300k cycles, ~150k redirects), so banked
instructions survive several times longer. LESSONS explicitly
recommends bundling the queue with the IF predictor next.

Rough model: back-end stall cycles ~0.14 per instruction, 78% of them
bank an instruction (~0.11/instr); with redirects now ~3% of
instructions instead of ~12%, survival rises from ~45% (r4s1's
implied rate) to ~75-80%, i.e. ~0.08 cycles/instr hidden out of a
CPI of ~1.45 -> roughly -5% to -6% cycles.
