hypothesis.hypothesis:
Part A (IPC, predictor/branch-resolution). An aligned conditional branch
(instr[8]==0) whose rs1 or rs2 matches the rd of a LOAD in ID/EX no
longer takes the load-use bubble. hazard_unit: load_use_hazard is
qualified with !(IF/ID is aligned BRANCH) -- precompute a 1-bit
`ifid_br_ok` flop in IF/ID at capture (predecode of the fetch word,
same as the existing br_ok) so the new term is one flop input on the
existing compare LUT, and do NOT add it to the ID/EX datapath enable
(r7s2's C3 cone). ID marks the instruction `late` (ID/EX control flop,
cleared by flush) and records which operand(s) come from the LOAD
(late1/late2 = the fwd?_ex match with id_ex_mem_read). In EX a `late`
branch produces NO redirect and no BHT training (its sel_* are forced to
0 in ID, so EX's redirect AND-OR is untouched), and EX/MEM captures
extra flops: late, late1/late2, the non-load operand values (post
forward rs1/rs2 already exist as EX/MEM.rs1_val/rs2_val), late_sel_*
(= the ID one-hot selects, prediction folded in), alt_target, pc[10:2],
bht_ctr, pred.
MEM stage (branch in EX/MEM, LOAD in MEM/WB): operand = late? ?
MEM/WB.wb_data : EX/MEM.rs?_val (flop-selected 2:1), 32-bit eq + one
33-bit borrow compare, late_sel_* AND-OR -> late_mis. late_mis lands in
exactly ONE flop, late_q (reset 0, D = late_mis && EX/MEM.valid &&
!hold_mem_wb). late_tgt_q <= EX/MEM.alt_target unconditionally (no
compare on its enable). Nothing else reads late_mis combinationally.
Cycle m+1 (late_q = 1): late_q is a flop side input to (1) ovr_d
(ovr_d = redirect || late_q || (ovr_q && !imem_ready)), (2) the
ovr_tgt_q D-mux select (late_q ? late_tgt_q : redirect_target; both
flop-sourced / the existing path gets one flop-selected 2:1), (3) EX
kill (kill = ovr_ex_q || late_ex_q copy), (4) ID flush (ovr_id || late_id_q
copy), (5) the MEM-stage instruction (the one that was in EX at m):
gate io_dmemWEn / io_dmemREn, ex_mem_mem_op into hazard dmem_stall,
and MEM/WB valid/reg_write with a late_mem_q copy. Use separate
syn_preserve copies of late_q per consumer group (like ovr_q's).
In cycle m+1 the redirect of the EX instruction is suppressed by kill
and div_unit start by kill, as today. At m+2 ovr_q is set and F fetches
late_tgt_q from imem (existing override path). A late mispredict thus
costs 4 cycles vs 1 bubble + 2 today (+1 net), a correct late branch
saves the full bubble. BHT training for a late branch comes from a
registered late_bht_we/idx/wdata written at m+1; if EX's registered
training fires in the same cycle, the late one wins (lost EX update
only costs accuracy). RVFI: MEM patches the late branch's rs?_val with
wb_data and its pc_next with late_mis/actual direction when capturing
MEM/WB (RVFI-only, pruned by synthesis).
Correctness corner cases (formal will hit them):
(a) a misaligned LOAD traps and does not write rd, so the late operand
must fall back to the older value: EX captures, for late operands, the
lower-priority forward (MEM/WB wb_data or ID/EX rs?_val, skipping the
EX/MEM source that holds the load's address) into EX/MEM (flop -> 2:1
-> flop, off the ALU cone), and MEM uses wb_data only when
MEM/WB.ctrl.reg_write is set (a flop select). (b) the younger instruction
X1 that sat in EX at m may be a DIV that already started div_unit
(kill was low at m); add an `abort` input to div_unit (late_q copy)
that returns it to IDLE and clears result_q. (c) late_q must be a
one-cycle pulse; the branch in MEM is never a mem op, so no dmem stall
can hold it at m.
Expected: -105k bubbles + ~8k extra (7.5% of late branches mispredict,
+1 cycle each) = ~-97k cycles (~-2.7%, to ~3.465M; r8s2 measured
~-127k with an extra-cycle-free variant).
Part B (Fmax, port r8s0 verbatim from its implementation_notes in
log.jsonl): L0 fill written one cycle late from staging flops (no LUTRAM
write data/address from the imem->predecode->carry-select cone), the
64-bit data RAM split into a next-PC RAM and an instruction RAM with
their own syn_preserve read-index copies, 6-bit tag with the L0 limited
to PCs < 32 KiB. r8s0 measured median 93.94 MHz vs 92.32 at 3,563,948
cycles. Build Part B first, run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench
--all-options` to confirm the ~94 MHz median, then add Part A and
re-time: Part A must not appear on any of the top paths (the only new
combinational logic is MEM/WB.wb_data -> compare -> late_q, one flop,
~same depth as today's EX compare but with flop-only inputs on the
other side).
Combined: ~+1.7% Fmax x ~+2.8% IPC = ~+4.5%.

Wire late_q copies to IF (ovr_d, ovr_tgt mux), ID flush, EX kill, MEM gating, hazard unit, and the late BHT training port.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-003-r9s2 (regression, -1.85%): The late load->branch resolve was built in the registered form LESSONS asked for, on top of r8s0's L0 trim: the MEM compare lands only in late_q, and its syn_preserve copies are flop side inputs to ovr_d, the ovr_tgt_q select, EX kill, ID flush, the dmem-stall term and a div_unit abort. title: Five-cone micro-cut of r9s0's measured top tier: per-source IF incrementers/BHT index, flat DSP sign bit, 5-term redirect with late BHT training, div0 off result_q
motivation:
I re-timed the champion (r9s0) on all three place options with
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 30` before
proposing this. Options 1 and 2 set the 96.718 MHz median and have
identical reports. Their top 25 paths lie within 0.13 ns
(15.634 -> 15.504 ns arrival) and fall into five distinct cones:
  C1 IF fetch mux (paths 1,3,4,6-8,11-15,18,25): cpu/u_if/ovr_pc_q ->
     fetch_pc = ovr_pc_q ? ovr_tgt_q : pc_q -> {30-bit pc_inc carry
     chain (27-28 cells) | BHT index -> 512x2 LUTRAM -> bht_ctr} -> pt ->
     pc_d -> pc_q / data_q.alt_target / idx_{tag,ins,vld}_q.
  C2 ALU (paths 2,5,10): data_q.opb_val_31 -> alu_b[31] -> DSP sign bit
     ({b[31]&mul_b_signed,b}) -> DSP -> mul_hi mux -> out mux ->
     alu_result (6 cells, 15.632); sa_rf/sa_wb -> alu_a -> adder ->
     11-way case -> out mux (15.627 / 15.591).
  C3 L0 hit (path 9): idx_tag_q -> tag LUTRAM -> 6-bit compare -> hit
     -> fetch_ok -> pc_en (CE of ~58 flops) -> pc_q_16 (15.594).
  C4 EX redirect (paths 16,17,24): data_q.s1_rf -> rs1 forward AND-OR ->
     cmp_eq/cmp_lt/cmp_ltu -> 7-term redirect_raw -> {pred^redirect_raw
     -> ctr_new -> bht_wdata (15.572, 11 cells) | ovr_d -> ovr_l0_q
     (15.508)}. In option 0 this cone is the worst path (15.954).
  C5 div_unit (paths 19-23): u_div/b_q -> (b_q == 0) SETUP
     div-by-zero -> result_q (15.522, 10 cells).
LESSONS r5s0/r8s0/r9s0: at this period the next untouched cone sets the
gain, so a >4.6% micro-opt has to cut every tied cone in one iteration.
Every cut below keeps the cycle count (3,563,948) unchanged.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Lower every cone above 15.1 ns (about 0.5 ns off the 10.34 ns period)
with local, IPC-neutral rewrites:
(1) C1 IF: stop routing the ovr_pc_q fetch mux into the long cones.
    - pc_inc gets per-source incrementers that start at flops:
      pc_inc = ovr_inc_q ? (ovr_tgt_q + 1) : (pc_q + 1). ovr_inc_q is a
      new syn_preserve same-D copy of ovr_q, so the 2:1 select lands
      after the carry chain and not in front of it.
    - The BHT read index gets its own copies: bht_idx_q (a same-D copy
      of pc_q[10:2], loaded from pc_d[10:2] under pc_en like the L0
      idx_*_q copies) and ovr_bht_q (an ovr_q copy):
      bht_ctr = bht[ovr_bht_q ? ovr_tgt_q[10:2] : bht_idx_q]. The index
      fanout into the 32 RAM16 blocks is then split off from imem_addr
      and the adders.
    - lo_sum / pc_hi_p1 / pc_hi_m1 read a fetch_pc copy selected by a
      third ovr copy (ovr_add_q). imem_addr keeps ovr_pc_q.
    All of these are same-D copies of non-RVFI nets, the pattern that
    passed formal with the ovr_q, fwd_wb_q and L0-index copies (r7s0's
    problem was different-D copies of the RVFI-observed regfile address).
(2) C2 ALU: ID registers the signedness into the selects that build the
    DSP's 33rd operand bits: sb_ex_s = sb_ex & mul_b_signed (the same for
    wb/rf, and for the A side). EX forms a33 / b33 as their own flat
    3-source AND-OR, as deep as every other operand bit, so the extra
    sign LUT in front of the DSP goes away. Also fold div_in into the
    nonmul tree's last OR and keep the post-DSP mux flat, as LESSONS
    r5s0 advises: `mul_sel ? mul_out : nonmul_or_div` stays a single
    flop-selected LUT3 per bit, with `(* syn_keep = 1 *)` on nonmul so
    synthesis cannot re-associate it after the DSP.
(3) C3 L0 hit: compute in_range from a registered in_range_q copy. It is
    updated beside pc_q from pc_d[31:15] == 0, which is precomputed on
    the ptgt and pc_inc sides (each side's upper 17-bit zero test is
    registered or computed in parallel before the pt select), so hit =
    valid & in_range_q & tag_eq. Also split pc_en into two syn_keep
    copies, one for pc_q and one for the four idx copies plus bht_idx_q,
    to halve the CE fanout.
(4) C4 redirect: one 33-bit magnitude compare replaces cmp_lt/cmp_ltu.
    Operands are {rs1[31]^sgn, rs1[30:0]} vs {rs2[31]^sgn, rs2[30:0]},
    and sgn is an ID-registered flop (BLT/BGE). ID merges the one-hot
    selects into sel_lt/sel_ge, so redirect_raw is a 5-term AND-OR and
    each rs1/rs2 forward bit loses a comparator load (LESSONS r9s0 part
    D). BHT training is registered one level earlier: EX registers
    br_taken_act = pred ^ redirect_raw and bht_ctr into flops, and
    ctr_new is computed from those flops on the write port. That drops
    the bht_wdata endpoint (C4's worst in options 1/2) and leaves
    redirect_raw with only the ovr_* D inputs as fanout. The BHT write
    lands one cycle later, which is performance-only (a one-cycle-older
    counter on back-to-back reads of the same branch, which r9s1 showed
    is IPC-neutral).
(5) C5 div_unit: remove the SETUP div-by-zero early exit (the real,
    non-ALTOPS branch). Restoring division by 0 already gives quo = all
    ones and rem = |a|. Only the signed quotient negation needs gating:
    neg_quo_q <= (a_neg ^ b_neg) && (b_q != 0), a single-flop endpoint.
    neg_rem_q = a_neg already makes REM x/0 = a. result_q then loads
    only in FIX, DONE-consume and reset, so the b_q==0 -> result_q
    cone is gone. A divide by zero now takes 32 more cycles (CoreMark
    never divides by zero). The ALTOPS SETUP->DONE branch stays as it
    is. test_alu.py / the div cocotb vectors (div-by-zero, INT_MIN/-1)
    must still pass.
Estimate: if each cone drops 0.4-0.6 ns, the median goes 96.7 -> about
101-103 MHz at unchanged cycles, i.e. +4.5% to +6.5%. The risk is a
sixth cone just below 15.50 ns that the 25-path report does not show.
The implementer should re-run `--all-options --paths 60` after each
group and keep a group only if the 3-option median does not fall.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r10s0 (regression, -0.99%): Cutting all five cones of r9s0's measured top tier in one iteration, as r8s0/r9s0 advised (the top 25 paths of median options 1/2 lie within 0.13 ns: IF ovr_pc_q -> fetch mux -> pc_inc/BHT index, opb -> DSP sign bit, L0 hit -> pc_en, forward -> lt/ltu -> redirect/bht_wdata, div b_q==0 -> result_q), with IPC-neutral local rewrites (per-source incrementers and more ovr_q/BHT-index copies, ID-registered a33/b33 selects behind a syn_keep nonmul|div net, a registered in_range_q and split pc_en, one 33-bit compare with an ID-registered signedness bit and BHT training from EX flops, no divide-by-zero early exit) scored 268.68 against 271.38, about 95.8 MHz if cycles stayed at 3,563,948 (inferred; no per-option timing, cycle count or implementer notes were recorded, and the truncated diff shows only the ALU, redirect and div groups, so whether each group was kept only when the median rose is unknown), so the ~0.5 ns per-cone saving the estimate assumed never appeared; the likely reason (inferred) is that each cut trades one LUT level for more flops, copies and fanout (a second 30-bit incrementer, three more ovr_q copies, bht_idx_q, in_range_q, two pc_en nets), and in a top tier this flat a one-level saving is lost in the place-and-route shuffle, as r9s1's per-source IF adders and late BHT training also gained nothing; so treat ~96.7 MHz as a plateau for LUT-level micro-cuts on this core line, stop re-proposing IF per-source duplication and flop-sourced BHT training, look for the next gain in IPC or a structural change at a stage boundary, and land any further micro-cut alone, keeping it only if the 3-option median rises.

title: Move all branch/JALR resolution from EX to MEM (single resolve point); load->branch pairs lose their bubble
motivation:
Champion r9s0: 271.38 = 10 x ~96.7 MHz / ~3.564M cycles for 2,922,015
retired instructions (CPI 1.22, ~642k lost cycles). The two biggest
loss items the trace data in log.jsonl names are (1) load-use bubbles:
203,959 adjacent LOAD->consumer pairs, 135,320 (66%) of them a
conditional BRANCH, and (2) the EX redirect cone, which is the
champion's worst path (clock -> u_ex -> u_if, 10 cells: EX 3-source
forward AND-OR -> eq/lt/ltu comparators -> sel_* AND-OR -> ovr_d ->
the five ovr_q copies).
Three earlier attempts (r7s2, r8s2, r9s2) ADDED a second, MEM-stage
resolve for load-fed branches on top of the EX one, so every late
consumer (EX kill, ovr_tgt select, load-use compare, dstall term)
landed on cones already tied at the top, and all three lost 4-9% Fmax.
This hypothesis is structurally different: it MOVES the one and only
branch/JALR resolve point from EX to MEM and deletes the EX
comparators and the EX redirect entirely, so there is still exactly
one redirect source feeding ovr_d, and it starts at low-fanout flops.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the pipeline so conditional branches and JALR resolve in
MEM (EX/MEM register) instead of EX:

1. EX no longer compares. EX/MEM already captures the post-forward
   rs1/rs2 (rs1_val/rs2_val, today RVFI-only and pruned) and the AGU
   sum (mem_addr = JALR target). Add to EX/MEM: the sel_* one-hot
   mispredict selects, pred, bht_ctr, alt_target, jalr_ok
   (= is_jalr && !agu1, registered), and two late-forward selects
   lf1/lf2 (see 3). All of these are flop-to-flop copies from ID/EX.
2. MEM resolve: op1 = lf1 ? fwd_br_q : EX/MEM.rs1_val (one LUT3, all
   flops), same for op2; one eq + one lt + one ltu compare; the same
   flat AND-OR as today's EX redirect with the sel_* flops, plus
   jalr_ok, gated by !ovr_mem_q. That is the only input to ovr_d.
   The target mux is flop-selected: EX/MEM.is_jalr ? mem_addr[31:2]
   : alt_target[31:2] -> ovr_tgt_q (captured every !ovr_q cycle, as
   now). A branch in MEM is never a memory op, so no dmem stall can
   coincide with its redirect (the !stall qualifier disappears).
   fwd_br_q is a new syn_preserve same-D copy of MEM/WB wb_data
   (same D / reset / !hold_wb enable as fwd_wb_q), so the EX forward
   copy's fanout is not touched (r9s0/r9s2 lesson).
3. Load->branch without a bubble: IF/ID carries a registered is_br
   predecode bit (already computed in F as is_br; one extra IF/ID
   flop). hazard_unit's load-use term becomes
     id_ex_mem_read && !if_id_is_br_q && (rd==rs1 || rd==rs2) && rd!=0
   (one flop input into the existing final AND). The branch enters EX
   right behind the LOAD, takes the load's address as its (stale)
   EX-forwarded value, and in MEM overrides it from fwd_br_q, which
   then holds the load's data (the load is in MEM/WB). ID computes
   lf1 = s1_ex && id_ex.mem_read (and lf2) and registers it into
   ID/EX, EX copies it into EX/MEM. Distance-2 loads and all ALU
   producers are already correctly forwarded in EX, as today.
4. Wrong-path kill now spans three stages. In the override cycle the
   instruction in MEM (the one right behind the branch) is killed by a
   new ovr_mem_q flop copy (same D as the other ovr copies): it gates
   dmem_wen / dmem_ren, the dmem_stall term (!ready && mem_op &&
   !ovr_mem_q stays one LUT4), wb_rw_next, and MEM/WB valid/reg_write
   capture. EX kill (ovr_ex_q) and ID flush (ovr_id_q) are unchanged.
   div_unit gets an abort (= ovr_ex_q flop) that returns it to IDLE,
   since a DIV right behind a mispredicted branch now starts one cycle
   before it is killed.
5. RVFI: pc_next, branch_taken, the misaligned-branch trap and the
   rs1/rs2_rdata of a late-forwarded branch are computed in MEM from
   the true outcome and registered in MEM/WB (RVFI-only, untimed).
   BHT training moves to MEM (still registered one cycle late).

Cycle model: +1 cycle per mispredict and per JALR (39,772 + 13,735 =
+53.5k), -1 cycle per load->branch pair (-135.3k) => about -82k
cycles (-2.3%). Fmax: the champion's worst cone (EX forward AND-OR ->
comparators -> redirect -> ovr) is deleted from EX; its replacement
starts at flops whose only loads are the comparator (a LUT3 2:1 mux
instead of the 6-input 3-source AND-OR, one level shorter), and EX's
rs1/rs2 nets lose the comparator fanout, which relieves the
rs1 -> AGU -> mem_addr path. Expect +2-4% Fmax (the ALU forward cone,
~0.02 ns behind, becomes the limiter), so about +4-6% fitness.
Must be checked with the 3-option median
(`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`) and cosim cycles
(`--bench --istall --dstall`). Before submitting, run insn_beq/insn_blt,
insn_jalr, pc_fwd and liveness from checks_si.cfg (the kill window
grows to three stages), and a cocotb case with LW -> BNE on the loaded
register, a store directly behind a mispredicted branch (must not
write), and a DIV directly behind a mispredicted branch.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-002-r10s1 (regression, -2.55%): Moving the only branch/JALR resolve point from EX to MEM (EX comparators and redirect deleted, a single ovr_d source driven from EX/MEM flops, a separate syn_preserve fwd_br_q wb_data copy for the late load operand, and an IF/ID is_br flop exempting load->branch pairs from the load-use bubble) scored 264.45 against r9s0's 271.38, about 92 MHz if cycles fell by the modeled ~82k or 94 MHz if they did not, against 96.7 MHz (inferred; no timing report, cycle count or implementer notes were recorded), so moving the resolve point lost Fmax just as the three versions that added a second MEM resolve did (r7s2, r8s2, r9s2); the likely reason is that deleting the EX redirect cone cannot raise Fmax when r10s0 measured five cones tied within 0.13 ns, while the three-stage kill puts a new ovr_mem_q copy on cones that were never on the branch path (dmem_wen/ren, the dmem-stall term, the hazard unit, MEM/WB capture and wb_rw_next, which feeds ID's registered forward selects and, per the diff, now EX too) and adds the s1_wbr/s2_wbr misaligned-load fallback selects and a div_unit abort ORed into the result_q reset, and the net cycle win was at most ~2.3% because the extra cycle on each of the ~53.5k mispredicts and JALRs gives back ~40% of the 135k load->branch bubbles; so retire the whole load->branch bubble family on this core line, including moving the resolve point, because its net cycle saving is too small to pay for any new consumer on the kill or stall cones.

title: Single-source MEM-stage branch/JALR verify from dedicated flops (EX redirect cone deleted, load->branch bubble gone) + 8-entry IF return stack
motivation:
The champion (r9s0, 96.718 MHz median [93.8, 96.7, 96.7], 3,563,948 cycles)
has its worst path on the EX redirect cone: u_mem/fwd_wb_q_18 -> EX forward
AND-OR -> eq/lt/ltu comparators -> sel AND-OR -> !stall/!kill -> ovr_d ->
u_if/ovr_l0_q (10 cells, 15.954 ns). The comparators hang off the same
forwarded rs1/rs2 nets as the AGU / write-data paths, and the result fans
into five ovr_q copies plus the BHT training flop.
Trace data in log.jsonl (ISS, timed window, 2,922,015 insns):
  - 529,588 branches, bimodal mispredicts 39,772; 13,735 JALR, all
    returns (an 8-entry RAS hits 13,734). Today each costs 2 cycles.
  - 135,320 of the 203,959 adjacent LOAD->consumer pairs have a
    conditional branch as the consumer: ~135k load-use bubble cycles
    (3.8% of the run) that no direction predictor removes.
Direction-predictor headroom is exhausted (gshare up to 2K entries only
reaches ~32.6k mispredicts). The only predictor-side lever left is WHERE
the prediction is verified. Every earlier attempt at the load->branch
bubble (r5s2, r7s2, r8s2, r9s2) ADDED a second, late redirect source next
to the EX one and put the MEM compare on the shared MEM/WB wb_data net;
r6s2 (single MEM source, 4.079M vs 4.189M cycles, -2.6%) lost Fmax
because its MEM compare also read MEM/WB.wb_data directly, which was then
the EX ALU forward source (its worst path became wb_data -> ALU,
16.47 ns). r9s0 has since given EX a private syn_preserve forward copy
(fwd_wb_q), so the cause of r6s2's loss can now be avoided structurally.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move ALL control-flow verification from EX to MEM, as the ONLY redirect
source, computed from dedicated low-fanout flops. EX no longer has any
comparator or redirect. Keep the r9s0 pipeline otherwise unchanged.

1. EX (ex_stage.sv): delete cmp_eq/cmp_lt/cmp_ltu, redirect_raw,
   redirect, redirect_target and the BHT training block. EX/MEM gains
   (all plain flops, captured on !stall like the rest of reg_q):
     - br_a_q / br_b_q (30..32 bit): the post-forward rs1 / rs2 (these are
       the same values reg_q.rs1_val / rs2_val already register for RVFI,
       but use SEPARATE syn_preserve copies so the compare flops are not
       the RVFI/MEM-WB fanout nets);
     - late1_q / late2_q: the operand came from s?_ex AND the producer now
       in EX/MEM is a LOAD (EX/MEM.ctrl.mem_to_reg) -> the forwarded value
       is stale; compute from flops in ID (s1_ex && id_ex mem_read is known
       when ID/EX captures) and register through ID/EX -> EX/MEM;
     - the one-hot sel_* (prediction already folded in, unchanged ID
       logic), is_jalr, pred, pred_ret, bht_ctr, alt_target (pc+4 or
       pc+imm), ras_tgt (predicted return target), agu1 (JALR misalign).
   The JALR target is EX/MEM.mem_addr (already = agu_sum, registered).
2. MEM (mem_stage.sv): the verify cone, all from EX/MEM + a NEW dedicated
   syn_preserve copy of MEM/WB wb_data (br_wb_q, same D/hold as
   fwd_wb_q, fanout = only the two late-operand muxes; NOT reg_q.wb_data
   and NOT EX's fwd_wb_q):
     opa = late1_q ? br_wb_q : br_a_q ; opb = late2_q ? br_wb_q : br_b_q
     eq, one 33-bit borrow compare (signedness = flop from ID) -> lt
     mis_br  = AND-OR(sel_*_q, {eq,!eq,lt,!lt})
     mis_jr  = is_jalr_q && (agu1_q ? pred_ret_q
                             : !(pred_ret_q && mem_addr[31:2]==ras_tgt_q))
     redirect_mem = (mis_br || mis_jr) && ex_mem.valid && !kill_mem && !dmem_stall
     target = (is_jalr_q && !agu1_q) ? mem_addr[31:2] : alt_target_q[31:2]
   (a predicted-ret JALR that turns out misaligned goes to pc+4 = alt).
   This cone is flop -> flop-selected 2:1 -> compare -> AND-OR -> ovr_d:
   one forward level (2 LUT4) shorter than today's EX cone, with private
   sources. The 2:1 only exists for load-fed branches; others read flops.
   BHT training moves here (registered one cycle late as today).
3. Kill: the redirect still only sets IF's ovr_q/ovr_tgt_q flops. In the
   ovr_q cycle three wrong-path instructions are squashed: IF/ID (ID
   flush, as today), ID/EX (EX kill, as today) and EX/MEM, via a new
   syn_preserve ovr copy kill_mem_q: gate dmem_wen/dmem_ren, the
   dmem_stall term (ex_mem_mem_op && !kill_mem_q), MEM/WB valid /
   reg_write capture and wb_rw_next. Mispredict penalty becomes 3 cycles.
   div start is gated while EX/MEM holds an unresolved branch/JALR
   (flop condition), so a wrong-path DIV never starts (no div_unit abort).
4. hazard_unit: load_use_hazard ignores an aligned BRANCH in IF/ID, using
   a predecode flop br_q carried in IF/ID (imem_ready ? br_ok : l0_br_ok,
   already computed in IF), ANDed with id_ex_mem_read at LUT level 1 in
   parallel with the rd compares (no new level on the load-use cone).
   JALR, stores and ALU consumers keep the bubble.
5. IF return-address stack: 8 x 30-bit SHIFT-REGISTER stack so TOS is a
   flop (no read mux). Predecode `ret` (jalr x0,0(x1) or 0(x5); exact
   match on the imem word, L0 stores a ret bit in prd_mem). Next PC:
     pc_d = pt ? ptgt : (ret ? tos_q : pc_inc)
   ret/tos only enter the non-critical input of the existing final LUT3,
   ptgt stays a single level. IF/ID/ID-EX/EX-MEM carry pred_ret and
   ras_tgt; for a ret alt_target = pc+4. Updates are non-speculative, at
   MEM when EX/MEM moves into MEM/WB (valid && !kill_mem_q && !stall):
   push pc+4 on JAL/JALR with rd in {x1,x5}, pop on ret. 3-cycle update
   latency only misses rets within 3 fetch slots of their call (rare).
Cycles (vs 3,563,948): -135k load->branch bubbles, +40k (+1 cycle per
branch mispredict), -27.5k (returns 2 -> 0 cycles) => about -115k to
-120k (-3.2..-3.4%; r6s2 measured -2.6% on an older base with the same
mechanism). Fmax: the current worst cone is deleted; its replacement is
1-2 LUT levels shorter with private sources, and EX's rs1/rs2 lose three
comparator loads, so the period falls to the next tier (ALU cone), est.
+1..+3%. Net about +4..+6%.
RVFI-only fields (pruned by synthesis, so free): EX can no longer know a
branch's outcome, so branch_taken, the misaligned-taken-branch trap
(taken && imm[1] -> is_illegal, pc_next = pc+4) and the branch pc_next
move to MEM using the MEM compare; for a late operand MEM/WB.rs?_val must
be replaced by reg_q.wb_data (the true loaded value), since EX/MEM holds
the stale forwarded load address.
Guard rails for the implementer (from LESSONS): never read reg_q.wb_data
or fwd_wb_q from the MEM compare; do not add any term to EX redirect
(there is none); stage every new RAM/flop write from flops; run
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` and cosim before
submitting, plus insn_beq_ch0 / insn_jalr_ch0 / pc_fwd formal checks.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-003-r10s2 (regression, +0.94%): The cleanest MEM-only branch/JALR verify built so far scored 273.94 against r9s0's 271.38, the first of six load->branch attempts to beat the champion but far under the 4.6% bar (it compared from dedicated br_a/br_b EX/MEM flops, used a private syn_preserve br_wb_q copy that ID-computed late1/late2 flops select only for load-fed operands, and added an 8-entry shift-register IF return stack verified in MEM), and sibling r10s1's logged numbers for the same move without the return stack (3,487,640 cycles, only -2.1%, at a 92.23 MHz median, worst path now ID sb_wb -> EX ALU alu_result at 16.24 ns) explain the ceiling: deleting the EX redirect cone does not raise Fmax, because the ALU forward cone of the flat top tier sets the period while the three-stage kill still costs a little, and r10s2's ~3.6% edge over r10s1 is the return stack's ~1% cycle cut (13.7k returns at 2-3 cycles each) plus about 2.5% better Fmax from the flop-sourced compare, putting it at ~94.4-94.8 MHz, still below 96.7 (inferred; no cycle count or timing report was recorded for this iteration); so the family's ceiling on this core line is about +1%, stop re-proposing it, and reuse the return stack only as a small IPC add-on bundled with an orthogonal Fmax cut, verified where it adds no term to a top-tier cone.

title: Non-blocking stores: a dedicated dmem port register lets a store whose bus cycle stalls retire and drain later, so the pipe freezes on dmem only for loads
motivation:
LESSONS puts the r9s0 champion (271.38, ~96.7 MHz, ~3.564M cycles for
2,922,015 instructions) on a flat top tier: r10s0 cut all five tied cones
and lost, and the load->branch family is retired. The next gain has to be
IPC that adds nothing to those cones. Of the ~642k overhead cycles, dmem
stalls are the largest share (~250k from r5s2's trace study, against
~135-160k load-use, ~110-160k redirects and ~100k leftover istall).
The bench draws dmem_ready at random every cycle (xorshift, 100/128
accept), whether or not a request is pending. So a mem op in MEM waits
0.28 cycles on average, and today the whole pipe freezes for it
(dmem_stall = !dmem_ready && EX/MEM mem op). Loads have to wait because
their data is needed. A store does not: nothing in the pipe needs it,
and the bus is idle in ~70% of cycles. Yet every stalled store currently
freezes the front end, ID, EX and MEM. No prior iteration has touched
the store side of dstall (grep log.jsonl: no store buffer, no
non-blocking store).

LESSONS puts the r9s0 champion (271.38, ~96.7 MHz, ~3.564M cycles for
2,922,015 instructions) on a flat top tier: r10s0 cut all five tied cones
and lost, and the load->branch family is retired. The next gain has to be

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the dmem port from the EX/MEM register. Add dedicated port flops in
EX, loaded on the same edge that EX/MEM captures an instruction:
port_addr_q (= agu_sum), port_wdata_q (byte-replicated rs2), port_wen_q
(byte mask, gated with !misalign), port_ren_q and port_wr_q/port_rd_q (1-bit
op flags). They are computed in EX from agu_sum[1:0] (the 2-bit low
sum, as agu1 already does), mem_width and the ID/EX mem_read/mem_write
flops, gated with !kill (ovr_ex). They are the only drivers of
io_dmemAddr/WData/WEn/REn. The address is still a single flop whose D
is agu_sum, so Gowin keeps absorbing it into the dmem BSRAM address
register exactly as it absorbs EX/MEM.mem_addr today. EX/MEM.mem_addr
stays as it is for load alignment, the misalign trap and RVFI.

Port enable: port_en = dmem_ready || !(port_rd_q || port_wr_q), so the
port holds while its op is pending, and is a LUT3 of flops like today's
stall term. While the port holds, its D input is the EX instruction (or
no-op).

Stall rules (hazard_unit), all from flops:
  dmem_stall = !dmem_ready && (port_rd_q ||
               (port_wr_q && id_ex_memop && !ovr_ex))
- A load in MEM whose cycle stalls freezes the pipe exactly as today
  (port_rd_q implies the load is still in EX/MEM).
- A store in MEM whose cycle stalls does NOT stall anything. It moves on
  to MEM/WB and retires (RVFI reports its addr/wmask/wdata from the
  pipeline as now), and its write stays on the port until the first
  cycle with dmem_ready=1.
- The next mem op that reaches EX while that write is still pending
  triggers the ordinary full freeze (EX/MEM, ID/EX and IF/ID hold;
  MEM/WB keeps its data with valid cleared). In the cycle the store
  drains, it advances into EX/MEM and the port loads its address on
  the same edge, so a load after a store to the same word always reads
  the new data.
id_ex_memop = mem_read | mem_write | (FENCE/EBREAK in EX), as one ID/EX
control flop cleared like the others. This keeps EBREAK, which ends
cosim, and FENCE from passing a pending store, so the last UART/marker
write cannot be lost.
Using a full freeze, rather than holding only EX and bubbling EX/MEM,
keeps ID's registered forward selects valid: their invariant is that
EX/MEM and MEM/WB move whenever ID/EX does. The !ovr_ex term means a
wrong-path mem op in EX during an override cycle is killed and never
frozen, so kill still takes effect in that cycle. In an override cycle,
EX/MEM holds a branch or a bubble, so port_rd_q is 0 and the load term
cannot fire either.

Expected effect: a stalled store costs 0 cycles instead of ~1.28 unless
the very next instruction is also a mem op (back-to-back store bursts
in prologues are not helped). Estimate: stores are ~25-30% of mem ops,
so ~65-80k of the ~250k dstall cycles; about 55-65% of those hidden
gives ~40-50k cycles. Add the shorter freezes when a pending store
overlaps a later load stall. That is about -1.3 to -2% cycles.
Fmax should be unchanged: the dmem address is still one flop with an
enable from three flops, and dmem_stall grows from a LUT3 to a LUT5 of
flops. That stays well behind the load-use compare in backend_stall.
The byte mask, misalign check and wdata replication move from MEM into
EX after agu_sum[1:0] and the rs2 forward. Both are short, and they come
off the dmem BSRAM-output side of MEM.
This alone is below the 4.6% bar. It is the micro_opt diversity
entry: a pure-IPC change on the largest remaining cycle bucket, with
only flop-driven control. If it holds Fmax, it stacks with any later
Fmax cut.

changes.description: Add dmem port flops (port_addr_q <= agu_sum, port_wdata_q <= replicated rs2, port_wen_q <= byte mask & !misalign, port_ren_q, port_rd_q, port_wr_q) with enable port_en = dmem_ready || !(port_rd_q || port_wr_q), D gated with in.valid && !kill. Compute misalign / byte mask from the 2-bit low AGU sum (rs1[1:0] + imm[1:0]) and mem_width. Export the port signals to core.sv. EX/MEM register unchanged (keeps mem_addr for RVFI and load alignment); its stall input is the new dmem_stall.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r11s0 (regression, -5.47%): Non-blocking stores, built as dedicated EX port flops that alone drive the dmem bus (port_addr_q from agu_sum next to EX/MEM.mem_addr, plus byte mask, misalign gate and wdata replication moved from MEM into EX after the rs2 forward and the AGU low bits, port_rd/wr_d gated with the kill flop, a port_en hold from io_dmemReady, and an id_ex_memop && !ovr_ex term added to dmem_stall), scored 256.54 against r9s0's 271.38, which puts median Fmax at about 91.4 MHz if cycles did not move or ~89.6-90.2 MHz if they fell the expected 1.3-2%, against 96.7 MHz (inferred from fitness ~ 10 x MHz / Mcycles; no timing report, cycle count or implementer notes were recorded), so a 5.5-7.5% Fmax loss swamped a cycle gain capped at ~2%; the likely reason is that every new term landed on the flat top tier that r10s0 measured: the forwarded rs1/rs2 and agu_sum nets that start the ALU forward cone gained a second 32-bit address register and the EX-side lane/replication logic, and the ovr_ex kill copy gained loads on both the port D logic and the pipe-wide stall/hold; so on this ~96.7 MHz core an IPC change worth <=2% cycles must add no load to EX forward/AGU nets or to the kill/stall nets, and store-side dstall should be retried, if at all, only as a write-pending latch behind MEM fed from EX/MEM flops, leaving EX untouched.

title: Merge MEM into EX: AGU moved to ID, dmem accessed in EX from the ID/EX address flop (5-stage, load-use bubble replaced by an address interlock)
motivation:
Champion r9s0: 271.38 = 10 x ~96.7 MHz / ~3.564M cycles for 2,922,015
retired instructions (CPI 1.22, ~642k lost cycles). LESSONS r10s0 calls
~96.7 MHz a plateau for LUT-level micro-cuts (five cones tied within
0.13 ns), and six load->branch attempts (r5s2..r10s2) show that any
second or later resolve point costs more Fmax than it saves. Yet the
load-use bubble is still the largest cycle loss after the dstall:
203,959 adjacent LOAD->consumer pairs (135,320 of them a conditional
branch), ~5.7% of all cycles. All those attempts kept the memory
access one stage after EX and tried to move the branch to the data.
This hypothesis moves the data to the branch instead. It is a stage-boundary change (the kind
r10s0's lesson asks for): the dmem access happens in the same stage
as the ALU, so a load's data is in a register as early as an ALU
result. Branch resolution, the redirect, ovr_q and the kill
machinery all stay where they are.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the back end from ID -> EX -> MEM -> WB to ID(+AGU) -> EX(+dmem)
-> WB, i.e. the classic "address generated in decode" pipeline:

1. ID computes the load/store effective address rs1 + imm with its own
   32-bit adder fed by the regfile read (whose write-first bypass already
   covers distance 2, since WB writes the regfile from the new EX/WB
   register). It also computes misalign (from sum[1:0] and the width) and the byte
   mask. These go into ID/EX as mem_addr / misalign / byte_mask flops. io_dmemAddr is
   driven directly by ID/EX.mem_addr (still a plain flop Q, so Gowin
   keeps absorbing it into the dmem BSRAM address register, the same as
   EX/MEM.mem_addr today).
2. EX drives io_dmemREn / io_dmemWEn from ID/EX control flops ANDed with
   !misalign_q and !ovr_ex_q (a wrong-path load/store in an override
   cycle must neither write nor read OOB). Store data is the forwarded
   rs2 (existing flop-selected AND-OR) byte-replicated by mem_width.
   The loaded word is aligned/sign-extended in EX (dmem rdata -> shift ->
   sext, the same depth MEM has today) and registered into a separate
   EX/WB.ld_data field (plus a syn_preserve forward-only copy), so it
   does NOT join the ALU result mux, and the ALU cone is unchanged.
3. The MEM stage and the EX/MEM register disappear; EX/WB is the
   retirement/RVFI boundary and the regfile write port
   (w_data = mem_to_reg_q ? ld_q : alu_q, one LUT after flops, on the
   bypass side only). EX keeps a 3-source flop-selected forward:
   EX/WB.alu (s?_exa), EX/WB.ld (s?_exl) and the ID-read value. ID
   computes the selects exactly as today (match with ID/EX.rd, qualified by
   ex_rw_next, split by ID/EX.mem_read). The MEM/WB source is no longer
   needed because distance 2 reads the regfile bypass in ID.
4. hazard_unit: the load-use hazard is deleted. It is replaced by an
   address interlock: IF/ID holds a LOAD/STORE (optionally also JALR, see
   5), its rs1 equals ID/EX.rd, and ID/EX.reg_write is set -> one bubble.
   It uses the same flush/stall plumbing as today's load-use (bubble into ID/EX),
   and the predecode of "is mem op" from IF/ID opcode bits runs in parallel with
   the 5-bit compare. dmem_stall = !dmem_ready && (mem_read_q|mem_write_q)
   && !ovr_ex_q, using only ID/EX flops. On a dmem stall ID/EX and IF/ID hold, and EX/WB
   keeps its data but clears valid (today's hold_mem_wb discipline), so
   a stalled store/load still forwards from it.
5. (Optional, keep only if the 3-option median rises) JALR also takes its target from
   the ID AGU (ID/EX.mem_addr), with the same interlock. Then
   redirect_target = is_jalr ? mem_addr_q : alt_target_q is a pure flop mux and the agu1
   alignment bit is a flop, which takes the EX rs1+imm adder off the
   redirect -> ovr_q cone (one of the five tied top-tier cones).
6. Side simplifications from 2: a dmem stall can only happen when EX
   holds a memory op, never a branch/JALR/DIV. So the !stall term
   leaves the EX redirect, the BHT write enable and div_unit.consume (now 1).
   Together with the removed MEM stage, this takes the stall net off the
   redirect cone and removes ~200 MEM/WB flops plus the hold_mem_wb
   fanout.

Cycle model: every LOAD->consumer pair at distance 1 whose consumer
uses the value in EX (ALU op, branch, store data, MUL) loses its bubble.
That is most of the 203,959, including all 135,320 load->branch pairs. Pairs
where the load feeds the next load/store base (pointer chasing in
core_list_*) keep exactly one bubble, as today. The new cost is
ALU->address pairs at distance 1 (e.g. slli/add; lw). MEASURED with
test/cosim/reference.py on the -O3 2K CoreMark ELF over the timed
window (2,922,015 instructions, matching the champion exactly):
203,959 LOAD->consumer pairs at distance 1, of which 59,270 feed the
next load/store base (they keep their bubble), and 66,975 new
non-load->load/store-base pairs (no JALR pairs in either class). Net
-77.7k cycles (~-2.2%, 3.564M -> ~3.486M) as a first-order count, so
the cycle side alone does NOT clear the 4.6% bar. The hypothesis
needs about +2.5% median Fmax from the structural simplification (no
MEM stage, no stall term on the redirect/BHT/div cones, ~200 fewer
flops, optional flop-only JALR target). The mispredict penalty is
unchanged (branches still resolve in EX).
Fmax: the ALU forward cone, the IF cones and the L0 are untouched; the
redirect cone loses the stall term (and the JALR adder with 5). The
new risk is the ID cone IF/ID.rs1 -> regfile 32:1 read + bypass ->
32-bit AGU carry chain -> ID/EX.mem_addr / BSRAM address setup, which
replaces today's EX forward -> AGU -> BSRAM address cone (same adder,
regfile read instead of the forward mux in front of it). The implementer should
run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` and keep the change only
if the median holds at >= ~95 MHz.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-002-r11s1 (regression, -5.11%): Merging MEM into EX (an ID-stage rs1+imm AGU fed by the regfile read and registered as the dmem address, the dmem access and load align/sext moved into EX and written to a separate EX/WB.ld forward field, the load-use bubble replaced by a one-bubble base-register interlock, the JALR target taken from the ID AGU, and the stall term removed from the redirect/BHT/div cones) matched its cycle model almost exactly (about 3.487M cycles against the predicted 3.486M, -2.2%, inferred from fitness at the logged 89.8 MHz) but lost 7% of Fmax (89.8 against 96.7 MHz) instead of gaining the +2.5% the plan needed; the option-0 report shows why the "structural simplification" bought nothing: the new ID regfile -> AGU -> BSRAM-address path was not among the worst five, which were the old tied cones, all within 0.02 ns at ~16.43 ns (ID/EX s1_rf forward select -> EX branch compare -> redirect -> IF ovr_pc_q/ovr_l0_q at 35 cells, IF ovr_pc_q -> pc_q/alt_target, and the new EX/WB.ld select sa_exl -> ALU result), so deleting the stage, its ~200 flops and the stall term took no logic level off any of them, and the whole tier slowed by ~0.8 ns, probably from placement spread once the dmem BSRAM sat between the ID address flop and EX/WB and EX took on the load-align logic and a third forward source (LUTs rose to 5085 from 5048; the cause is inferred, since the implementer ran only option 0 and found no single new long path); so on this flat-tier core, removing a stall term or a whole stage is not an Fmax cut unless it removes logic levels from a top-tier cone, a stage-boundary move that relocates the dmem BSRAM disturbs the placement of the whole tier, and after seven failed load-use attempts (six load->branch resolve variants plus this one) the bubble's ~2% net cycle value cannot pay for any restructuring on this core line.

title: F-stage return-address stack, verified through the existing EX cmp_eq/sel_ne arm (no new EX redirect term)
motivation:
Trace data in log.jsonl (ISS, timed window, 2,922,015 insns) shows that
direction prediction is nearly saturated: the 512x2b bimodal BHT
mispredicts 39,772 of 529,588 branches, and gshare/tournament up to 2K
entries only gets to ~32k. The one large, clean predictor miss left is
JALR. All 13,735 JALRs in the timed window are returns, and an 8-entry
RAS hits 13,734 of them. Today every JALR redirects from EX: 2 bubbles,
plus about 0.28 extra cycles because an override cycle cannot use the L0
and has to wait for imem_ready. That is ~31k cycles, about 0.9% of
3,563,948.
r10s2 already built a RAS, but it verified returns at a new MEM-stage
resolve point, which paid the three-stage-kill Fmax cost. LESSONS says to
reuse the RAS only where it adds no term to a top-tier cone. This
hypothesis does that. Prediction happens in F and is selected by a flop.
Verification reuses the comparator and sel_ne arm that EX already has.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. RAS in F (if_stage.sv)
   - 8-entry stack: a top-of-stack flop plus a shift register or a
     circular pointer.
   - Push pc_inc on an accepted fetch of JAL or JALR with rd in {x1, x5}.
   - Pop on an accepted predicted return.
   - A return is predecoded from the word as exactly JALR x0, 0(x1) or
     JALR x0, 0(x5) (0x00008067 / 0x00028067), so imm = 0 and rs2 field = 0.
   - imem side: is_ret comes from imem_data, in parallel with the
     carry-select adder (it is shallower than the adder).
   - L0 side: one more predecode bit, ret_ok, is stored in the next-PC RAM
     at fill time. The fill is staged, as now.
   - pt gets an "|| ret" term, and ptgt becomes
     ret ? ras_top_q : (imem_ready ? tgt_imem : l0_tgt). ras_top_q is a
     flop, so this is a flop-side input on the last pc_d mux and does not
     add a level in front of the adder.
   - IF/ID carries pred_ret and the predicted target. alt_target stays
     pc + 4.
   - Repair: each fetched instruction carries a snapshot of the stack
     pointer down the pipe. In an override cycle, restore the pointer from
     the redirecting instruction's snapshot plus its own push/pop. Entries
     overwritten by a wrong-path push are tolerated: they only cost a
     mispredict.
2. Verify in EX with zero new redirect logic (id_stage.sv, ex_stage.sv)
   - A predicted return has rs2 field = x0, so its regfile rs2_data is 0
     and its s2_ex/s2_wb forward selects are 0 (s2_rf = 1).
   - ID ORs {pred_target, 2'b00} into ID/EX.rs2_val, through a flop-AND
     mask that is zero unless pred_ret.
   - ID sets sel_ne for the return (and leaves sel_eq clear), so the
     existing redirect_raw arm (sel_ne && !cmp_eq) fires exactly when
     rs1 != predicted target.
   - The `is_jalr && !agu1` redirect term is gated by a new flop,
     jalr_unpred_q (the old is_jalr_q AND !pred_ret). That keeps the same
     number of AND-OR inputs on the champion's worst cone
     (fwd_wb_q -> forward -> comparators -> sel AND-OR -> ovr_d ->
     ovr_*_q).
   - On a mispredicted return, redirect_target is still agu_sum (rs1 + 0).
     is_jalr_q keeps selecting it.
   - Misaligned rs1: rs1[1] = 1 can never equal the aligned prediction, so
     the arm fires. The target select becomes is_jalr_q && !agu1, so a
     trapping return goes to alt_target = pc + 4, which is the core's
     linear-PC trap convention. agu1 is a 2-bit carry and lands well
     before the agu_sum carry chain on the target mux, so the target cone
     is not lengthened.
   - BHT training stays gated to is_branch.
3. RVFI hygiene: for JALR, EX/MEM captures rs2_val as 0 and RVFI reports
   rs2_addr = 0. RVFI allows any rs2_addr for an instruction that does not
   read rs2, provided a nonzero address carries correct rdata. Zero/zero is
   always consistent, so the reg check never sees the substituted value.
   This logic is RVFI-only and pruned in the timed netlist.
   write_data (dmem) is irrelevant because a JALR never stores.
Cycle model: about -13.7k x 2 redirect bubbles, -3.8k override-wait
cycles and ~+0 new mispredicts, so ~-31k cycles (-0.9%). Fmax is meant to
be neutral. EX's redirect AND-OR keeps its input count, and the IF change
is a flop input on the final pc_d / ptgt mux. The residual risk is the
IF L0 next-PC RAM growing by one bit and the 3:1 ptgt mux on the IF
top-tier cone (ovr_pc_q -> fetch mux -> pc_inc/BHT index -> pc_d).
The implementer must run
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` and keep the change only
if the median holds at or above 96.7 MHz. Cosim must show cycles near
3.53M.
This is the diversity slot. The expected gain is honest and below the
4.6% bar, because the whole remaining predictor headroom (all mispredicts
+ returns) is only ~3% of cycles.

title: Register file in distributed LUTRAM (no reset loop, initial zeros): -16% LUTs, -47% FFs at measured-neutral Fmax
motivation:
The champion (r9s0: 5048 LUT4, 2101 FF, seeds 93.81/96.72/96.72 MHz) sits on a
flat top tier, and LUT-level cuts on those cones have stopped paying (r10s0).
The one large block not yet tried in another form is the register file:
1024 reset flip-flops plus two 32-bit 32:1 read muxes. r2s1 forced it into
flops to keep it out of BSRAM, but never tried distributed (async-read)
LUTRAM, which also keeps the read in ID and the rs?_val flops real.
The hypothesis was that removing that bulk would compact placement and lift
the tier, as dropping the fanout-1069 imem_ready net did in r4s2.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Mark regs[] (* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *). Drop the reset loop, which
LUTRAM cannot implement. Initialise the array to zero in an initial block, so
Verilator cosim and formal see the same start state the reset gave. Keep the

RVFI-observed address nets (r7s0 lesson: do not copy the regfile address).

  logic 5048 -> 4241 LUT, registers 2101 -> 1109, LUT-RAM 176 -> 208
  option 0: 93.811 -> 94.477 MHz (worst path ovr_tgt_q -> alt_target, 25 cells)
  options 1/2: 96.718 -> 96.694 MHz (worst path fwd_wb_q -> EX compare ->
  ovr_l0_q, 10 cells, 15.636 ns, tied within 0.05 ns with ovr_pc_q -> idx_prd_q
  and sb_rf -> ALU -> alu_result)
  median 96.694 MHz (unchanged), cycles expected identical.

in the EX-redirect -> ovr_q, ovr_pc_q -> F and forward -> ALU cones, not by
routing spread. This hypothesis is submitted as a measured, area-only
micro-opt. It frees ~800 LUTs and ~990 FFs for later IPC structures (a larger
or 2-way L0, a return stack, a store buffer) without moving Fmax. It is not
expected to clear the 4.6% bar alone.

     flow as a $mem with init, not as reset flops; r7s0 showed this check
     family can hang on regfile-read changes. If either check takes more
     than ~2 min, write that to the notes and stop.
  3. Run cosim (--bench --istall --dstall) and confirm the cycle count
     matches 3,563,948.

     implementation_notes.md whatever the outcome. Never revert silently
     (r11s2 lesson).

title: LUTRAM register file: replace the 1024-flop regfile and its two 32:1 read-mux trees with async distributed RAM (one RAM16SDP4 bank per read port)
motivation:
The champion (r9s0, 271.38, median 96.718 MHz, 3,563,948 cycles, 5048 LUT4 /
2101 FF / 176 LUTRAM) has stopped responding to cuts. r10s0 measured the
top 25 paths of the median place options within 0.13 ns across five
unrelated cones (IF ovr_pc_q -> fetch mux -> pc_inc/BHT index, opb -> DSP,
L0 hit -> pc_en, forward -> lt/ltu -> redirect, div b_q==0 -> result_q).
Cutting all five with LUT-level rewrites lost 1% (r10s0). Deleting a whole
cone or stage (r10s1, r10s2, r11s1) also bought nothing, because placement
moved and the whole tier slowed by ~0.8 ns. The reported worst paths are
6-10 logic cells long for ~10.3 ns of data path, so routing, not logic
depth, sets the period. LESSONS r10s0 says to look for "a structural
change", and a period this flat and routing-bound can only be moved by a
global change to the netlist's size and fanout, not by another cone cut.

The largest single block in the netlist is the register file. It has no
timing reason to be built the way it is:
  * 32 x 32 = 1024 flip-flops (49% of all 2101 FFs, about 512 CLS slots).
    They are forced into registers only to keep Gowin from using BSRAM,
    whose synchronous read absorbed the ID/EX flops (r2s0/r2s1).
  * Two 32-bit 32:1 read-mux trees, about 2 x 32 x 8 LUT4 plus a MUX2_LUT5..8
    ladder, roughly 500-550 LUT4 (~11% of the design).
  * A 31-way write-enable decode whose outputs drive 1024 CE pins, and 31
    flop D-pin loads on every MEM/WB wb_data bit.
  * A synchronous reset net fanning out to 1024 flops.
Gowin's distributed RAM (RAM16SDP4: 16x4, synchronous write, ASYNC read) is
the third option that r2s1 named but never built. It keeps the read
combinational in ID, so no ID/EX flop is absorbed (the BSRAM problem does
not come back), and it removes almost all of that storage and fanout. The
core already relies on the same primitive with the same access pattern
for the 512x2 BHT and the 128-entry L0 RAMs, and those passed formal and
timing.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rebuild reg_file.sv as async-read distributed RAM. Keep the module's ports,
the x0 arm and the write-first bypass byte-for-byte, so ID, RVFI and formal
see exactly the same nets. Pipeline topology, hazards and forwarding do
not change, so CoreMark cycles must stay at exactly 3,563,948.

1. Storage. One array, `(* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *) logic [31:0]
   regs [0:31]`, with a synchronous write
   `if (w_en && w_addr != 5'b0 && !reset) regs[w_addr] <= w_data;` and two
   async reads, regs[rs1_addr] and regs[rs2_addr]. Delete the
   `for (i..) regs[i] <= 0` reset loop: LUTRAM cannot be reset. Also add
   an `initial` zero-fill, which Gowin honours as the LUTRAM INIT and
   Verilator/yosys honour at time 0.
   Reset semantics stay exactly as today through a 32-bit "written"
   vector `wr_q` (flops, sync reset to 0, `wr_q[w_addr] <= 1` on every
   accepted write). A read of a register whose bit is clear returns 0, so
   every register still reads 0 after any reset, including a reset in the
   middle of a run. test_reg_file.py's reset_clears_all, multi-reset
   cocotb pipeline tests and the formal model then see the same behaviour
   as the flop regfile. This costs 32 FFs plus two 1-bit 32:1 muxes (~20
   LUT4), read in parallel with the LUTRAM. The `!reset` write gate makes
   sure no write can land while MEM/WB is still being reset.
   GowinSynthesis replicates a
   2-read-port async RAM into one RAM16SDP4 set per read port: 2 depth
   halves x 8 nibbles = 16 cells per port, plus a MUX2_LUT5 on addr[4].
   Check the synthesis report: LUTRAM should rise from 176 to about 208,
   and FF should fall by about 1024.
   Fallback, only if Gowin refuses to infer it and falls back to
   registers: two explicit arrays, bank_a read only by rs1_addr and
   bank_b read only by rs2_addr, both written identically, each marked
   `(* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram", syn_preserve = 1 *)` so they are
   not merged. Both banks must use the SAME rs?_addr / w_* nets that RVFI
   sees: no address copies (r7s0's formal hang came from different-D
   address copies).
2. Read side. Same structure as today, with the written-bit AND added:
     rs1_data = (rs1_addr == 0) ? 0 : (w_en && w_addr == rs1_addr) ? w_data
                                    : (regs[rs1_addr] & {32{wr_q[rs1_addr]}});
   (rs2 likewise). x0 still reads zero through the constant arm, not
   through the storage (r7s0 lesson). The written-bit AND folds into the
   existing bypass LUT (bypass select, w_data, RAM bit, written bit = 4
   inputs). The LUTRAM read is one LUTRAM level plus a MUX2_LUT5. Today's
   flop tree is LUT4 + MUX2_LUT5/6/7/8. The ID path IF/ID.instr -> read ->
   bypass -> opa_val/opb_val -> ID/EX therefore gets shorter or stays the
   same.
3. Write side. It is already flop-driven: w_addr = MEM/WB.rd, w_data =
   MEM/WB.wb_data, w_en = reg_write && valid. This follows the LESSONS rule
   that LUTRAM write ports must hang off flops, not off critical cones.
   Each wb_data bit drops from ~31 flop-D loads to 4 RAM DI pins. The
   31-output enable decode becomes 2 WRE nets.

Why Fmax should rise. Nothing on the five tied cones gains a level. What
changes is the placement problem: ~1024 fewer FFs, ~500 fewer LUT4s, and
no 1024-pin write-enable, reset or wb_data nets. The netlist shrinks by
~11% LUTs and ~49% FFs, and the ID/EX/MEM logic that the tied cones run
through (forward muxes, ALU, DSP, branch compare, ovr_q copies, IF) can
pack closer together. The tier is flat and routing-bound, and r4s2 showed
that removing a fanout-1069 net (imem_ready) lifted Fmax ~9% through
cones it never touched. Expected 96.7 -> ~101-103 MHz at identical cycles,
fitness ~284-288 (+5-6%).

Acceptance and measurement. Cycles must equal 3,563,948. If they do not,
the change is broken: it is meant to be a pure storage swap. Run
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` and keep the change only
if the 3-option median Fmax beats 96.718 MHz. Whether kept or reverted,
write to implementation_notes.md: the per-option Fmax, the LUT4 / FF /
LUTRAM counts, the worst 5 paths of the median option, and the cosim cycle
count, so the slot is never a null result (r11s2). Before submitting, run
at least insn_add_ch0 and reg_ch0 formal to confirm the solver time
matches the champion's.

title: F-stage return stack verified through EX's existing sel_ne/cmp_eq arm, landed unconditionally with measured median Fmax and cosim cycles
motivation:
Predictor headroom on the r9s0 champion (271.38, ~96.7 MHz, ~3.564M
cycles for 2,922,015 retired instructions) is small but measured. The
512x2b bimodal BHT mispredicts 39,772 of 529,588 branches, and
gshare/tournament up to 2K entries only reach ~32k, so direction
prediction is worth at most ~0.4% of cycles. Every one of the 13,735
JALRs in the timed window is a return, and an 8-entry RAS hits 13,734 of
them. Today each return redirects from EX: 2 bubbles, plus ~0.28 cycles
of override wait, because an override fetch cannot use the L0 and must
wait for imem_ready. That is ~31k cycles (~0.9%), the single largest
clean predictor miss left.
r10s2 built a RAS but verified it at a new MEM resolve point, which paid
the three-stage-kill Fmax cost. r11s2 proposed the zero-new-term version
below, but it produced a null result: no RTL diff, cycle count or timing
was recorded, most likely because the implementer reverted on the
"keep only if the median holds" gate. LESSONS asks for exactly this fix:
land the change, and record the measured median Fmax, the per-option
numbers, the worst path and cosim cycles, so the RAS is either proven or
retired.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict returns in F from a small return stack, select it by a flop on
the last pc_d / ptgt mux, and verify it in EX by reusing the existing
sel_ne && !cmp_eq redirect arm. This adds no input to the EX redirect
AND-OR and no level ahead of the IF carry-select adder.

1. RAS in F (if_stage.sv)
   - 4-entry stack: a top-of-stack flop ras_top_q plus 3 shift-register
     entries (push = shift down, pop = shift up). No pointer and no
     snapshot repair. Wrong-path pushes and pops only cost a mispredict:
     mispredicts are ~7.5% of branches, and CoreMark's call depth in the
     hot loops is <= 3. This keeps all RAS state off the redirect fanout.
   - Push pc_inc on an accepted fetch (pc_en) of a JAL, or of a JALR with
     rd in {x1, x5} (a call).
   - Pop on an accepted predicted return.
   - Return predecode is an exact word match: 0x00008067 (ret) or
     0x00028067 (jalr x0, 0(t0)). imm = 0 and the rs2 field is 0 by
     construction.
     - imem side: is_ret is computed from imem_data in parallel with the
       carry-select adder, and it is shallower than the adder.
     - L0 side: one more predecode bit, ret_ok, is stored in the next-PC
       RAM (prd_mem). It is written from the existing staged fill flops,
       so no RAM write port hangs off the imem cone.
   - pt gains an "|| ret" term. ptgt becomes
     ret ? ras_top_q : (imem_ready ? tgt_imem : l0_tgt). ras_top_q is a
     flop, so it is a flop-side input on the final mux.
   - IF/ID carries pred_ret. alt_target keeps meaning "where to go if
     the prediction is wrong". For a predicted return, the ID/EX
     predicted target is needed instead (next bullet), so carry
     pred_tgt = ras_top_q (30 bits) in IF/ID. Alternatively, reuse the
     alt_target field and mux in pc + 4 in EX's target select, which is
     already flop-selected.
2. Verify in EX with zero new redirect terms (id_stage.sv, ex_stage.sv)
   - A predicted return has rs2 field x0. So its regfile rs2_data is 0,
     and its s2_ex / s2_wb forward selects are 0 (s2_rf = 1).
   - ID drives ID/EX.rs2_val D = pred_ret ? {pred_tgt, 2'b00} : rs2_data.
     This is a 2:1 mux on a data flop D input. It can also be an OR,
     since rs2_data = 0 for these words.
   - ID sets sel_ne = 1 and sel_eq = 0 for a valid pred_ret. br_ok does
     not apply, because the instruction is not a branch.
   - The existing arm redirect_raw |= sel_ne && !cmp_eq then fires
     exactly when rs1 != predicted target. rs1 is forwarded as usual,
     and the target is rs1 + 0, with bit 0 cleared by JALR. A predicted
     target is always word-aligned, so if rs1[1:0] != 0, rs1 never
     equals it.
   - The `is_jalr && !agu1` term is gated by a new control flop,
     jalr_unpred_q = is_jalr && !pred_ret, replacing is_jalr_q in that
     AND term. It is cleared on flush/reset with the other control
     flops. The input count of the worst cone (fwd -> comparators ->
     sel AND-OR -> ovr_d -> ovr_*_q) is unchanged.
   - On a mispredicted return, redirect_target is still agu_sum[31:2]
     (is_jalr_q selects it), because rs1 + 0 is the true target.
   - Misaligned return target (rs1[1] = 1): the arm fires. Today a
     misaligned JALR traps and does not redirect, and pc_next = pc + 4.
     So the target select becomes (is_jalr_q && !agu1) ? agu_sum :
     alt_target, and alt_target must be pc + 4 for a predicted return.
     In that case EX redirects to pc + 4, the linear-PC trap convention,
     and the trapping return retires with pc_wdata = pc + 4. agu1 is a
     2-bit carry, early on the target mux.
   - pc_next / reg_write / misalign logic is unchanged. A JALR with
     rd = x0 writes nothing.
   - BHT training stays gated to is_branch.
3. RVFI hygiene
   - For a predicted return, EX/MEM.rs2_val captures the substituted
     predicted target. Report rs2_addr = 0 and rs2_rdata = 0 for JALR in
     the RVFI path. Gate EX/MEM.rs2_val with !is_jalr, or carry
     rs2_addr = 0, which it already is for these words.
   - This logic is RVFI-only and pruned in the timed netlist.
   - write_data (dmem) does not matter, because a JALR never stores.
4. Measurement protocol (mandatory, unlike r11s2)
   - Do NOT revert on an Fmax gate.
   - Run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` on the change.
   - Run cosim (`--bench --istall --dstall`) for the cycle count.
   - Write to implementation_notes.md:
     - the per-option Fmax and the median
     - the worst 5 paths of the median option
     - cosim cycles, and the number of returns predicted and
       mispredicted, if cheap to count
   - Also run formal insn_jalr_ch0, pc_fwd/pc_bwd and reg_ch0 before
     submitting.

Cycle model:
- returns: -13.7k x 2 redirect bubbles
- override waits that no longer happen: ~-3.8k
- RAS overflow/corruption mispredicts with 4 entries: ~+0.5k
- net: ~-31k cycles, ~-0.9%, to about 3.533M

Fmax: meant to be neutral within place-and-route noise. The EX redirect
AND-OR keeps its input count. The IF change is a flop input on the final
ptgt mux and one more predecode term on pt. Residual risk is the 3:1
ptgt mux on the IF top-tier cone (ovr_pc_q -> fetch mux -> pc_d) and one
more bit in the L0 next-PC RAM.

This is the diversity slot. The expected gain is honest and below the
4.6% bar, because all remaining predictor headroom (every mispredict
plus every return) is only ~3% of cycles. The value of this slot is a
measured verdict on the cheapest RAS form, so later rounds can bundle it
with an Fmax cut.

title: L0 loop cache 128 -> 256 entries with the valid bit folded into the tag LUTRAM (no valid-flop mux)
motivation:
Champion r9s0: 271.38 = 10 x 96.718 MHz / 3,563,948 cycles for
2,922,015 retired instructions (~642k lost cycles). LESSONS r10s0/r12s0
call ~96.7 MHz a plateau for LUT-level cuts, and the load-use, F-stage
RAS, store-buffer and MEM-resolve families are retired on this line, so
the remaining lever is a measured IPC chunk that adds no term to the
EX forward/redirect/kill/stall cones. The biggest such chunk is the
istall that the L0 misses: imem_ready is an independent ~22% draw, the
L0 hides about h x ~800k istall cycles, and r6s1's ISS trace measured
the per-fetch hit rate h at 71.5% (64 entries), 83.3% (128, today) and
93.8% (256). Going to 256 entries hides ~0.105 x 800k = ~84k more
cycles (-2.4%; r6s1 beat its own model by ~1%, so -2.4..-3.0%), and it
is a one-parameter change inside an IF-only module whose cones start
and end at IF flops.
The risk is the L0 read cone: r6s1 lost ~10% Fmax when the L0 first
went in (hit -> fetch_ok -> pc_en), and r8s0's trim took it off the top
tier but only by a small margin. Today the hit is
valid_q[idx] (a 128:1 mux of flops) AND tag_ram[idx] == tag; doubling
the depth doubles that flop mux (256:1, ~3-4 LUT/MUX2 levels plus 256
flops of fanout on idx_vld_q) and adds one MUX2 level to each LUTRAM
read. Folding the valid bit into the tag LUTRAM removes the flop mux
entirely, so the hit becomes one async LUTRAM read + one 6-bit compare,
which should keep the 256-entry hit cone no deeper than today's
128-entry one.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change only l0_icache.sv (and the IDX_W parameter / index-copy widths
in if_stage.sv):

A. IDX_W 7 -> 8 (256 entries, index pc[9:2], tag pc[14:10] = 5 bits;
   the L0 still only fills/hits for PCs below 32 KiB). if_stage's four
   syn_preserve index copies idx_tag/prd/ins/vld_q become [7:0] loaded
   from pc_d[9:2] (idx_vld_q is deleted, see B). Everything else in IF
   (fetch_ok, pt/ptgt/word muxes, ovr gating, fill staging) is
   unchanged.

B. Valid bit moves into the tag RAM: tag_mem becomes {v, tag[4:0]}
   (6 bits x 256, distributed_ram), written by the existing staged fill
   port as {1'b1, fill_tag_q}. hit = (rd == {1'b1, tag}) && in_range.
   The 256 valid flops and their 256:1 read mux are deleted.
   Flash-clear is replaced by a sweep: reset or flush (FENCE/FENCE.I in
   EX) sets sweep_q and clears an 8-bit sweep counter; while sweep_q is
   set the tag RAM write port writes {1'b0, x} at sweep_cnt_q every
   cycle (the write address/data mux sits on flop -> RAM WAD/DI only,
   never on a read cone), fills are dropped, and hit is forced to 0 by
   ANDing the registered !sweep_q into the compare (a flop side input
   to the existing last LUT of the hit equation). sweep_q clears after
   entry 255. A flush during a sweep restarts it. Correctness is
   unaffected: contents only affect performance, and no hit can occur
   while any stale entry may still be valid. Cost: 256 cycles of
   imem-only fetch after reset (before the start marker) and after each
   FENCE (none in the timed CoreMark loop). The tag RAM gets an
   `initial` zero fill too so simulation starts invalid.

C. Implementer protocol (mandatory, write to implementation_notes.md
   BEFORE any revert): run cosim (`--bench --istall --dstall`) and
   record cycles; run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`
   and record all three Fmax values, the median and the worst path.
   Decision rule: keep A+B if the 3-option median is >= 95.5 MHz. If
   the median falls below that and the worst path goes through the
   L0 (tag/prd/ins RAM -> hit/pt/ptgt -> pc_en/pc_d), try B alone at
   IDX_W = 7 (128 entries, valid-in-RAM) and record it as well, so the
   slot always reports measured numbers. If there is slack at 256 and
   time remains, also measure IDX_W = 9 (512 entries, tag pc[14:11]),
   where the hit rate should be ~97% (another ~-1% cycles), and keep
   whichever has the best fitness = 10 x median_MHz / Mcycles.

Expected: cycles 3.564M -> ~3.47-3.48M (-2.4..-3%), Fmax within
+-1% (the read cone gains one MUX2 level but loses the 128/256:1
valid flop mux and the idx_vld_q fanout), so fitness ~+2..+3%; with the
512-entry option measured ~+3..+4%. This is under the 4.6% bar on its
own unless the larger L0 beats the model like r6s1 did, so it is
proposed as the clean, isolated measurement of the last large IPC
chunk that touches no EX/MEM cone; if it lands near +3% it is the
IPC half to stack with the next Fmax cut.

title: Replace the 128-entry LUTRAM L0 with a 2K-entry BSRAM fetch cache read synchronously off the PC's D input (zero-bubble, covers the whole hot code)
motivation:
Champion r9s0: 271.38 = 10 x ~96.7 MHz / ~3.564M cycles for 2,922,015
retired instructions (CPI 1.22). Thirteen rounds of LUT-level cuts have
hit a flat ~96.7 MHz tier (r10s0, r12s0), and every IPC change that
touched EX, the kill/stall nets or the dmem BSRAM lost Fmax (r10s1,
r11s0, r11s1). The remaining stall budget is about 642k cycles: dstall
~250k, load-use ~160-200k (retired family), redirects ~110-160k and
leftover istall ~100-130k. The leftover istall is the one item whose
fix lives entirely inside the F stage and changes no EX, MEM, hazard or
dmem logic.

r6s1's ISS trace measured the direct-mapped fill-on-fetch L0 hit rate
as 71.5% at 64 entries, 83.3% at 128 (today) and 93.8% at 256, and
cycles tracked h x ~800k hidden istall almost exactly (3.552M measured
vs 3.58M modelled). So today ~0.167 x ~800k = ~130k cycles are lost to
L0 misses during !imem_ready. CoreMark's whole code image is a few KB,
so a cache that covers PCs below 8 KB (or 32 KB with a 2-bit tag) only
misses on compulsory first touches (~2-3k words over a 10-iteration
run, and only the ones that land in a !ready cycle cost anything).
A LUTRAM cache that big is impossible (the read mux depth would land on
the L0-hit -> pc_en and L0 -> ptgt -> pc_d cones, both in r10s0's top
tier). A GW2AR-18 has 46 BSRAMs and the bench uses ~4 for dmem, so
a 2048 x 72-bit fetch cache is 8 idle BSRAMs.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Structural change: turn the L0 from an async LUTRAM read indexed by
pc_q into a synchronous BSRAM read whose address register is a copy of
pc_q (same D = pc_d, same enable = pc_en), so the read crosses the clock
edge with the PC and its data is ready at the start of the fetch cycle,
like today's LUTRAM output, but for 16x the entries.

1. l0_icache.sv rewritten as `fetch_cache`: 2048 entries indexed by
   pc[12:2], each 67 bits {valid, tag = pc[14:13], instr[31:0],
   tgt[31:2], jal_ok, br_ok}, under `(* syn_ramstyle = "block_ram" *)`
   and written as an explicit synchronous read with enable:
     always_ff @(posedge clock) if (rd_en) rd_q <= mem[rd_idx];
   where rd_idx = pc_d[12:2] and rd_en = pc_en (exported from if_stage,
   the same nets that load pc_q), so it infers 8 SDPB blocks at
   2K x 9 with no LUT read mux. Keep an `initial` loop zeroing the
   array (valid = 0) for Verilator, formal (r12s0: an initialised $mem
   clears the formal checks) and the bitstream INIT. The reset-time
   address register is RESET_PC's index (load rd_idx with RESET_PC on
   reset via rd_en = reset | pc_en and rd_idx = reset ? 0 : pc_d).
2. Hit = rd_valid && rd_tag == tag_q && in_range_q && !collide_q.
   tag_q / in_range_q (pc[31:15] == 0) come from pc_q (flops; the
   17-bit NOR runs in parallel with BSRAM clock-to-out). collide_q
   guards the SDP read-during-write case (Gowin returns undefined data
   when the write port and read port hit the same address on one edge):
   register `fill_we_q && fill_idx_q == rd_idx` is NOT allowed (pc_d
   cone); instead keep a flop copy of the last written index and its
   write enable (wr_idx_l_q, wr_l_q, loaded when the RAM write fires)
   and compute collide = wr_l_q && wr_idx_l_q == rd_idx_q from flops
   (rd_idx_q = a 11-bit copy of pc_q[12:2] already available), which
   settles before the BSRAM data arrives. A collision costs one miss.
3. The fill path is unchanged in spirit: staged fill flops (fill_*_q)
   written one edge after the imem_ready fetch, as r8s0 established
   (no RAM write data or address straight off the imem/predictor cone).
4. Delete the 128 valid flops, the flash clear, the four syn_preserve
   idx_* copies and the 6-bit tag LUTRAM. FENCE / FENCE.I no longer
   clear the cache: imem and dmem are separate ports and stores cannot
   change code, so the cache contents only affect performance (the
   existing comment already states this); leave fence_ex unconnected or
   drop it from id_stage/core. Override cycles keep today's rule (no
   cache lookup, fetch_ok = imem_ready), so ovr_d gains nothing.
5. if_stage word/pt/ptgt selection is unchanged: word = imem_ready ?
   imem_data : c_instr, pt from c_jal_ok/c_br_ok and bht_ctr[1],
   ptgt = imem_ready ? tgt_imem : c_tgt, fetch_ok = imem_ready ||
   (c_hit && !ovr_l0_q). Only the source of c_* changes from LUTRAM
   to BSRAM data.

Why this should help: the ~130k cycles the 128-entry L0 still misses
during !imem_ready shrink to compulsory misses only, so cycles fall
to ~3.44M (-3.5%). The two L0 cones in the top tier get shallower:
today's l0_hit is idx_vld_q -> 128:1 valid mux AND idx_tag_q ->
LUTRAM -> 6-bit compare; the new one is BSRAM tco -> one LUT4 (valid,
2-bit tag, in_range_q, collide) -> fetch_ok, and c_tgt/c_instr come
out of the BSRAM with no 8:1 MUX2_LUT tree. Roughly 1000 LUT4 of
LUTRAM, the 128:1 mux and ~160 flops go away, so the IF region gets
less congested. The risk is BSRAM clock-to-out plus the column
routing back to IF, which must stay at or under today's LUTRAM
address->data->mux delay (~3 ns), and the new pc_d[12:2] ->
BSRAM AD loads (8 blocks).

Mandatory measurement protocol (r11s2/r12s2 produced null or
unexplained results because nothing was written down). Write
every number below to implementation_notes.md BEFORE deciding to keep
or revert:
  a. cosim cycles (`--bench --istall --dstall`) before/after and the
     new hit rate if cheaply countable;
  b. `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` median Fmax
     and the top-5 paths of the median option, noting whether any
     starts at a fetch_cache BSRAM;
  c. BSRAM / LUT / FF counts from the Gowin report (confirm the cache
     really mapped to 8 BSRAMs and not to LUTRAM/flops).
Fallbacks, in order, if the median Fmax drops more than ~2%: (i) halve
the fanout by going to 1024 entries x 72 bits (4 blocks at 1K x 18,
index pc[11:2], tag pc[14:12]); (ii) if the worst median-option path
starts at the cache BSRAM and ends at pc_q/idx flops, split the array
into two RAMs with private address-register copies (next-PC RAM
{valid, tag, tgt, jal_ok, br_ok} and instruction RAM {instr}) so the
pc_d -> AD fanout and the tco -> pc_d routes are separated, as r8s0 did
for the LUTRAM. Keep the change only if the 3-option median fitness
beats 271.38 by the 4.6% bar; if reverting, the notes from a-c above
must already be written.

title: Double the L0 next-PC predictor (BTB + word supply) to 256 entries, paid for by a LUTRAM regfile
motivation:
Direction prediction is exhausted on this core line. The 512x2b bimodal
BHT mispredicts 39,772 of 529,588 branches, and gshare/tournament up to
2K entries only reach ~32.6k (about 0.4% of cycles). The F-stage return
stack was retired after r12s2: one 30-bit mux level on the IF pc_d tier
cost ~3% Fmax, more than the 0.9% of cycles it saved. So the only
predictor structure with real headroom left is the one F uses in
imem-stall cycles. That is the L0 next-PC predictor, whose prd_mem holds
{predicted target, jal_ok, br_ok} per PC, a direct-mapped BTB that also
supplies the instruction word. When imem is not ready and this BTB misses,
F has no next PC or word and inserts a bubble. Of the champion's ~640k
overhead cycles, ~100-136k are these leftover istall bubbles. That is the
largest fetch-side loss left, larger than mispredicts plus returns
together (~122k incl. the override-cycle imem wait).
The r6s1 trace study on this exact binary (direct-mapped,
fill-on-every-fetch) measured a per-fetch hit rate of 71.5% at 64 entries,
83.3% at 128 and 93.8% at 256. Taking that hit rate from 83% to 94% hides
about 0.11 x ~800k = ~85k more istall cycles. r12s0 showed that the
LUTRAM register file is formal-clean and Fmax-neutral (96.718 -> 96.694 MHz
median) and frees ~800 LUTs and ~1000 FFs, and its lesson explicitly
recommends spending that room on a larger L0.

The r6s1 trace study on this exact binary (direct-mapped,
fill-on-every-fetch) measured a per-fetch hit rate of 71.5% at 64 entries,
83.3% at 128 and 93.8% at 256. Taking that hit rate from 83% to 94% hides
about 0.11 x ~800k = ~85k more istall cycles. r12s0 showed that the
LUTRAM register file is formal-clean and Fmax-neutral (96.718 -> 96.694 MHz
median) and frees ~800 LUTs and ~1000 FFs, and its lesson explicitly
recommends spending that room on a larger L0.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Two parts, landed in this order.

Part A: port r12s0's LUTRAM regfile verbatim. Use
`(* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *)` regs, an initial-block zero fill
instead of the reset loop, and keep the `rs?_addr == 0 -> 0` arm and the
write-first bypass on the RVFI-observed rs?_addr nets. Add no address
copies, because r7s0 showed that copies of RVFI-observed nets hang formal.
This part only makes room. Its scored effect was -0.03%.

Part B: raise l0_icache IDX_W from 7 to 8 (256 entries, 1 KiB of code).
- The tag becomes pc[14:10] (5 bits). The in_range limit (pc < 32 KiB)
  stays unchanged.
- Keep everything that r8s0/r9s0 proved: the staged fill (fill_*_q), the
  separate tag, next-PC (prd) and instruction RAMs, the four syn_preserve
  read-index copies (now 8 bits each), and lookup and fill disabled in
  override cycles.
- The only critical-cone growth should be one more MUX2 level (Gowin's
  hard MUX2_LUT8) in each LUTRAM read tree and in the 256:1 valid-bit mux.
  The hit -> fetch_ok -> pc_en path is one of the flat top-tier cones, so:
  1. Move the valid bits out of the 256:1 flop mux. Store a valid bit in
     the tag RAM as one more data bit ({valid, tag}, 6 bits, written by
     the staged fill).
  2. FENCE/FENCE.I flash-clear then needs an epoch. Keep a 1-bit
     epoch_q that toggles on flush. Write {epoch_q, tag} on fill, and hit
     requires rd_epoch == epoch_q. A flush flips the epoch, which
     invalidates every entry in one cycle. A single bit is enough only if
     stale entries from two flushes back cannot alias, so also run a
     background scrub counter after each flush. The scrub writes the
     inverted epoch into one tag entry per cycle where no fill is staged,
     and a second flush is held off (FENCE stalls in EX) until the scrub
     has covered all entries. CoreMark's timed window executes no FENCE,
     so the stall is never paid there.
     If this is too complex for the time budget, use the simple
     fallback: keep valid_q flops but split them into two 128-bit banks
     selected by idx[7] after the 128:1 muxes. The 7-bit index copies
     already exist, so this is the same depth as today plus one LUT3.
  This makes hit = (rd_tagv == {1'b1/epoch, tag}) && in_range. It is a
  6-bit compare straight off the RAM read (5 tag bits + epoch/valid),
  one bit narrower than today's 6-bit tag compare ANDed with a separate
  valid mux. So the hit cone gains at most the one MUX2 level in the RAM
  read and loses the valid-mux AND.
- The instruction and prd RAMs gain the same one MUX2 level. Their outputs
  feed only the word/pt/ptgt mux, which imem_ready selects as a flop.

Expected cycles: 3,563,948 -> ~3.48M (-2.3%), from ~85k istall bubbles
hidden at a 94% hit rate (fewer if conflict misses inside the hot kernels
dominate). Fmax: neutral to -1% if only one MUX2 level lands on the hit
cone, and 0 if the epoch-in-tag form removes the valid mux. Net expected
+1 to +3%. This probably cannot clear the 4.6% bar alone. It is the
largest prediction-supply gain that adds no logic to the pc_d mux, the EX
redirect or the kill/stall nets.

MANDATORY measurement protocol (r11s2/r12s2 produced null results without
it):
1. Before any edit, run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`
   on the unchanged core. Record the per-option Fmax and the worst path in
   implementation_notes.md.
2. After Part A, and again after Part B, run the 3-option timing plus
   cosim (`--bench --istall --dstall`). Record the cycle count, all three
   option Fmax values, the median and the worst path of each option.
3. If Part B lowers the 3-option median by more than 1%, try the
   valid-bank fallback before giving up. Write every number down before
   any revert.
