title: Cut all four tied top-tier cones at their high-fanout nets: BHT in BSRAM read off pc_d, per-byte select-flop copies, hazard-only rs copies
motivation:
I ran `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` on the unchanged
r13s1 champion. Options 1 and 2 both give 100.874 MHz and set the median.
Option 0 gives 88.146 MHz. In options 1/2 the top 12 paths lie within
0.015 ns (arrival 15.19-15.21 ns, required 10.294). They fall into four
cones. Each one is dominated by ROUTING out of a high-fanout net, not by
logic depth:
  A  ID/EX sa_rf (fanout 32, 1.451 ns route) -> alu_a AND-OR (2 LUTs,
     fanout 72, 1.094 ns route) -> DSP A (3.760) -> alu_result_s3 ->
     alu_result_s (2 LUTs, 0.898 + 0.563 ns routes) -> EX/MEM.
  B  ID/EX s1_wb (fanout 32, 2.140 ns route) -> rs1 fwd LUT -> 7-LUT
     compare/redirect tree ovr_d_s58..s0 -> ovr_q/ovr_l0_q/ovr_pc_q/
     ovr_id_q (fanout 5, 1.052 ns route).
  C  pc_q[3] -> fetch_pc mux imem_addr_3 (fanout 37, 1.977 ns route) ->
     BHT LUTRAM RAD (0.517) -> 5-level MUX2 tree bht_DOL_* -> pt_s2 ->
     pt_s0 (fanout 61) -> pc_d_s2 (fanout 9, 1.329 ns) -> L0 BSRAM ADB.
     The 512x2 distributed-RAM BHT read sits on the pc_d cone.
  D  IF/ID data_q.instr_24 (FANOUT 519, 3.093 ns route) -> load-use
     compare (n124_s2 COUT) -> n300_s1 -> reg_write_q_s2 (the shared
     stall/backend_stall net, FANOUT 255, 1.604 ns) -> accept_s0 (fanout
     96, 1.229 ns) -> IF/ID payload CE.
LESSONS (r10s0) say one-LUT micro-cuts on a flat tier get lost in P&R.
These are different. Every cone carries 1.5-3 ns of route out of nets
with fanout 32-519, plus one removable 2.6 ns LUTRAM read (C). Cutting
all four together is the only way a flat tier moves.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Four IPC-neutral cuts in one iteration, one per cone. Build them in the
order C, D, A, B.

C (pc_d cone, largest): move the BHT out of distributed RAM into a
  block-RAM BHT that reads exactly like l0_icache. It gets a synchronous
  read whose address register loads the PC's own D (pc_d) with the PC's
  own enable (pc_en), so bht_ctr comes from BSRAM clock-to-out at the
  start of the fetch cycle. This removes the fetch_pc mux, its fanout-37
  route, the RAM16 read and the 5-level MUX2 tree from the
  pt -> pc_d -> BSRAM-address cone. Make it 2048 x 2 indexed by pc[12:2]
  (the same index as the L0, still well under one 18 Kb BSRAM, with less
  aliasing than 512). Widen bht_widx to 11 bits (EX flop of in.pc[12:2]).
  Keep the write port on EX flops as today. A read-during-write collision
  only returns a stale or undefined 2-bit counter, which is never a
  correctness issue. Initialise to weakly-not-taken as now.
  Override cycles fetch from ovr_tgt_q while the BHT read is indexed by
  pc_q, exactly as the L0 already is. In an ovr_l0_q cycle, predict an
  aligned imem-side BRANCH with static BTFN (imem_data[31], i.e. a
  backward target is taken) instead of bht_ctr[1]. JAL is still always
  taken. ID/EX gets bht_ctr from the BSRAM read as before. In an override
  cycle that counter belongs to pc_q, so training from it is merely
  approximate, which only affects performance. This touches only the
  ~53k override fetches. Expect <0.1% cycles. L0-side predictions
  (non-override cycles only) are unchanged.

D (IF/ID CE cone): give the hazard unit its own copies of the IF/ID rs
  fields. Add `(* syn_preserve = 1 *)` hz_rs1_q/hz_rs2_q, loaded with
  word[19:15]/word[24:20] under the same `accept` enable as data_q.instr
  (same-D copies like ovr_q/fwd_wb_q, which passed formal; NOT the
  regfile read address, which stays on instr[19:15] per r7s0). Compute
  accept's backend_stall from a separate syn_keep'd load-use compare on
  these copies, so the IF/ID enable no longer shares the fanout-255 ID/EX
  stall net. Keep hazard_unit's existing compare (on the instr bits) for
  stall_id/flush_id unchanged. Optionally split accept into two
  syn_preserve-free LUT copies (data_q CE vs valid_q/pc_en) to halve its
  fanout of 96.

A (ALU/DSP cone): (1) duplicate each EX forward-select flop
  (s1_*/s2_*/sa_*/sb_*) into 4 syn_preserve copies, each driving one byte
  lane of its AND-OR, so no select flop drives 32 LUTs across the die.
  (2) Give the multiplier its own syn_keep'd copy of the alu_a/alu_b
  AND-OR, which feeds only the DSP A/B pins. The shared alu_a net
  (fanout 72: adder, shifter, compare, DSP) stays for the non-MUL tree.
  (3) Make the post-DSP select a single flat level: ID registers one-hot
  mul_lo_q / mul_hi_q, and nm_g = (nonmul | div_in) & !mul_sel is kept
  under `(* syn_keep = 1 *)`, giving
  out = ({32{mul_lo_q}} & p[31:0]) | ({32{mul_hi_q}} & p[63:32]) | nm_g.
  That fits one LUT4+MUX2_LUT5 after the DSP instead of two routed LUTs.
  Keep the ALTOPS branch in alu.sv consistent: under ALTOPS mul_out
  replaces the product halves in the same flat select.

B (redirect -> ovr cone): the per-byte select copies from A also feed the
  branch comparator's rs1/rs2 forward LUTs. Give the comparator dedicated
  syn_keep'd rs1_c/rs2_c AND-ORs that feed only cmp_eq/cmp_lt/cmp_ltu,
  off the AGU/write_data fanout. Also split ovr_d into two identical
  syn_keep'd LUT copies: one feeding ovr_q/ovr_pc_q/ovr_l0_q in the IF
  region, one feeding ovr_ex_q/ovr_id_q. That cuts the 1.052 ns final
  route.

Fmax: removing ~1-2.5 ns of route/LUTRAM from each cone should lift the
flat tier by at least ~0.5-0.7 ns before the next tier binds: 9.91 ns ->
~9.3 ns, about 106-108 MHz at the median. Cycles stay ~3.44M (BTFN in
override cycles is noise, and the 2048-entry BHT may help slightly).
Expected +5% (low confidence: the next tier below 15.19 ns is unseen
because the report lists only the top 12).

MANDATORY measurement protocol: write every number to
implementation_notes.md before any revert.
1. Baseline (already measured above): options 0/1/2 = 88.146 / 100.874 /
   100.874 MHz.
2. After C, then after C+D, then after all four, run
   `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options --paths 20`. Record
   all three Fmax values, the median and the worst 5 endpoints of option
   1. Keep a group only if the 3-option median does not fall.
3. Run cosim (`--bench --istall --dstall`) once at the end and record the
   cycle count (baseline 3,442,936). Run formal insn_add_ch0 and reg_ch0
   after D to confirm the hazard copies do not stall the solver.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r14s0 (regression, -4.48%): Cutting r13s1's four route-dominated top-tier cones together by replication and relocation (the 512x2 LUTRAM BHT moved into a 2048x2 BSRAM read off pc_d/pc_en with static BTFN in override cycles, syn_preserve hz_rs1/hz_rs2 copies feeding a separate load-use compare for the IF/ID enable, each of the 12 EX forward selects split into four per-byte syn_preserve flops, a syn_keep DSP-only copy of the alu_a/alu_b AND-OR with a flat mul_lo/mul_hi/nm_g output select, and, per the hypothesis though the truncated diff does not show them, comparator-only rs1/rs2 AND-ORs and two ovr_d copies) scored 279.85 against 292.99, a median of about 96.4 MHz if cycles stayed near the measured 3,442,936 (BTFN and the bigger BHT should move them well under 1%), against 100.874, so the core fell back to just below r9s0's ~96.7 MHz plateau instead of reaching the ~106-108 MHz estimate (inferred from fitness = 10 x MHz / Mcycles; no implementation notes, per-group medians or cosim cycles were written despite the mandatory protocol, so which group cost the Fmax is unknown, and the "keep a group only if the median does not fall" gate was either skipped or misapplied); the likely reason (not timed) is that replication moves fanout upstream instead of removing it: the extra DSP and comparator operand AND-ORs add loads to every forwarded data bit (the wb_data forward copy, EX/MEM result, rs1/rs2_val) that starts the same cones, the 36 extra select flops and the hazard copies spread the EX and IF/ID regions, and the new BHT BSRAM hangs a second block-RAM address port, at a fixed BSRAM column site, on the pc_d net that cone C was meant to shorten; so on Gowin, route delay out of a high-fanout net in the timing report does not mean that hand-duplicating the net or its consumers will help, and on this core any fanout split should land alone, timed over all three place options, rather than in a four-cone bundle whose loss cannot be attributed.

title: Producer-side operand bypass: forward into the ID/EX operand flops, leave EX with only a LUT3 load bypass
motivation:
For eight scored iterations in a row, every logged worst path has started
at the EX operand-forwarding mux. Its heads were ID/EX forward-select or
forward-data flops: r13s1 (the champion) at data_q.s2_wb, r13s0 and
r12s2 at s1_rf, r9s0 at fwd_wb_q, r10s0 and r10s2 at opb_val, and r10s1
at sb_wb. These paths end in two cones that tie at the top of the tier:
  - forward -> 32-bit eq/lt/ltu compare -> redirect AND-OR -> ovr_d ->
    ovr_q/ovr_l0_q copies (the champion's worst path, 16.64 ns on option 0)
  - forward -> ALU (adder/shifter/case mux) -> alu_result
The AGU -> dmem address path also starts at the same mux.
Today each EX operand is a 3-source one-hot AND-OR
(s?_ex & ex_mem.alu_result | s?_wb & fwd_wb | s?_rf & val). That is
6 inputs, which takes two LUT4 levels (or LUT4 + MUX2_LUT5) on Gowin,
plus three select flops per operand, each with fanout 32. 12 select
flops drive 128 operand bits.
The micro-cuts have plateaued (r10s0: per-cone LUT-level trims are lost
in placement). The forwarding topology itself has never been changed:
r3s1 moved only the distance-2 bypass into ID, and it lost because it
put dmem BSRAM -> load align in series in front of the ID/EX flops. This
proposal moves the bypass to the producer side for every producer whose
value comes from a flop or from the ALU, but keeps the load-data bypass
in EX. That way the BSRAM path is not lengthened.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change where operands are bypassed. Today the consumer muxes them at the
start of EX. Instead, write them into the consumer's ID/EX operand flops
at the end of the cycle in which the producer computes them. Each EX
operand then becomes one LUT3: `ld ? fwd_wb : op_q`.

Let instruction I be in ID in cycle t. When I reaches EX at t+1:
  - Distance-1 producer P1 (in EX at t): its value is the EX ALU output
    alu_out in cycle t (combinational, including div_in and the MUL
    select). ID muxes alu_out into I's operand D input with select s_ex,
    which keeps today's qualification: ex_rw_next && rs != 0 &&
    id_ex_rd == rs. A load P1 is already a load-use bubble, so it never
    forwards here.
  - Distance-2 producer P2 (in EX/MEM at t):
      * If P2 is not a load (ex_mem.ctrl.mem_to_reg == 0), its value is
        the flop ex_mem.alu_result. ID muxes it into the operand D input
        with select s_mem = wb_rw_next && !ex_mem.mem_to_reg && match &&
        !s_ex.
      * If P2 is a load, its data exists only after the dmem BSRAM
        (r3s1's losing path). Keep that one bypass in EX: set a registered
        flag s_ld = wb_rw_next && ex_mem.mem_to_reg && match && !s_ex, and
        in EX take fwd_wb (the existing syn_preserve MEM/WB wb_data copy)
        when the flag is set.
  - Distance 3 or more: unchanged. The regfile write-first bypass
    supplies it in ID.

ID operand D-path, per operand (rs1_val, rs2_val, opa_val, opb_val):
  pre  = s_mem ? ex_mem.alu_result : base   // base = rf / pc / imm as today
  op_d = s_ex  ? alu_out           : pre
The masking by use_pc/use_imm is the same as today's sa_/sb_ masking:
pc and immediate operands never forward. The s_ex mux sits after
alu_out. Have synthesis merge it with the ALU's final
`mul_sel ? mul_out : (nonmul | div_in)` LUT. Write the op_d mux so that
alu_out is its late input. Do not add a separate priority level. pre is
computed early from flops.

EX: rs1 = s1_ld ? fwd_wb : rs1_q, and the same for rs2, alu_a and alu_b,
each a LUT3 with a per-operand select flop (fanout 32). The comparators,
AGU, ALU, write_data, div_unit operand latch and RVFI rs?_val all read
these LUT3 outputs. Everything else in EX is unchanged: the redirect
equation, kill, BHT training, misalign.

Why this is structural and not a micro-cut: it deletes the 3-source
forward network that heads every logged top-tier path. The 12 x 32 select
fanout becomes 4 x 32 load-only selects, and the forward-select flops
s?_ex/s?_wb/s?_rf/sa_*/sb_* disappear. In exchange the ALU output gains
one late merge into the next instruction's operand flops. Net effect by
cone:
  - Redirect -> ovr cone: about one LUT level and a 32-fanout select
    shorter.
  - AGU -> dmem address: shorter by the same amount.
  - ALU cone: about level-neutral at worst. It loses a 2-level AND-OR at
    the start and gains about one MUX2/LUT at the end.
IPC is unchanged: same bubbles, same forwarding coverage. Cycles must
stay at exactly 3,442,936. Any change in the cycle count means a
forwarding bug.

Correctness argument, already relied on today (id_stage comment): every
edge on which ID/EX captures a real instruction also advances EX/MEM and
MEM/WB.
  - dmem stall freezes ID/EX, EX/MEM and MEM/WB together, and fwd_wb holds.
  - div_stall holds ID/EX. The consumer in IF/ID re-evaluates op_d every
    cycle and captures on the cycle the DIV leaves, when alu_out carries
    div_result in DONE.
  - A load-use bubble turns P1 into a distance-2 load on the next cycle,
    which goes through s_ld.
  - A fetch-override kill of EX coincides with the ID flush.
div_unit still latches its post-bypass operands in IDLE.

Implementation protocol (mandatory, write it to implementation_notes.md
before any revert):
  1. Build. Then run cosim with `--bench --istall --dstall` and check that
     cycles equal 3,442,936 exactly.
  2. Run one formal check that ties rs?_rdata to the regfile
     (insn_add_ch0) and also reg_ch0. Run these before the full formal
     suite.
  3. Run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` and record the
     per-option Fmax, the median and the worst path of each option.
Gate: keep the change only if the 3-option median beats 100.874 MHz.
If the ALU cone (alu_out -> op_d) becomes the new worst path, try
`(* syn_keep = 1 *)` on `pre`, so the late mux stays a single LUT3 after
alu_out.
Second risk: the ID regfile read path (IF/ID instr -> 32:1 regs mux ->
write-first bypass -> pc/imm pre-select) gains the two flop-selected
LUT3s. Its selects come from 5-bit compares of flops and arrive early.
If this path shows up in the top paths, fold the s_mem arm into the
regfile's existing write-first bypass level: rf_data is
`w_en && w_addr == rs ? w_data : regs[rs]`, so add ex_mem_alu as one
more priority arm there. Do not add a separate level after the
pre-select.
Distinct from r3s1, which put dmem BSRAM -> load align -> mux in front of
ID/EX. Here load data never enters ID. The only combinational producer
value that crosses into ID is alu_out, and it lands on a single late
LUT3.

title: Block-RAM BHT with two read-address registers (PC-D copy + redirect-target copy), 2K entries
motivation:
r13s1's lesson: on Gowin, a lookup table of 128+ entries on the
pc_en/pc_d cone belongs in BSRAM addressed from the PC's own D/enable.
Moving the 128-entry L0 there gave +7.96%, and most of that was Fmax
(about 100.9 MHz, 3,442,936 cycles). The 512 x 2-bit bimodal BHT is
the last deep async LUTRAM still on that cone. It accounts for all 32
LUTRAM cells in the r13s1 report. Its read path is
ovr_pc_q -> fetch_pc mux (fanout ~45) -> 9-bit address into 32
RAM16SDP4 -> 32:1 MUX2_LUT5..LUT8 tree -> bht_ctr[1] -> pt ->
30-bit pc_d select -> pc_q D and the L0 BSRAM read address. That is
about as deep as the 128-entry LUTRAM L0 hit cone that r13s1 deleted,
and the r12s0/r13s0 reports put this IF fetch_pc -> pc_d tier at the
top. Its write port is also a u_ex -> u_if path (bht_we/widx/wdata
flops -> 32 LUTRAM WREs).
Measured on the champion (make timing, option 0, 88.15 MHz): path 1
is s2_wb -> EX compare -> ovr_l0_q (16.639 ns). Paths 2-4 are ALU
result cones within 0.04 ns of it. Path 5 (16.596 ns, 11 cells) is
ovr_tgt_q -> fetch_pc -> ... -> L0 BSRAM read address, i.e. the IF
fetch_pc -> pc_d tier this change shortens. Its 11-cell count fits
the BHT LUTRAM read better than the carry-select chain. So in
option 0 this cut alone cannot move Fmax, because the EX/ALU cones
are tied above it. Any gain has to come from options 1/2, where IF
may be at the top. Hence the low confidence.
Trace data in log.jsonl (2,922,015 insns): direction-predictor
headroom is tiny. Bimodal 512 mispredicts 39.8k of 529.6k branches,
and gshare/tournament only reach 32.6k-36k. All predictor-related
losses together (about 80k mispredict cycles, 27k return cycles,
about 15k override-istall cycles) are about 3.5% of cycles. So the
predictor slot can only clear the bar by taking predictor logic off
the fetch-timing tier, not by predicting better. LESSONS also rules
out new mux levels on pc_d (r12s2 RAS: -2.2%) and deeper async reads
(r13s0: -1.5%). This hypothesis removes levels from pc_d instead.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the async-LUTRAM BHT with a synchronous block-RAM BHT whose
read data is ready at the start of the fetch cycle. Use exactly the
L0 trick: the read address register is a copy of a flop the fetch
already uses.

1. Copy A (normal fetch): `(* syn_ramstyle = "block_ram" *)`, 2048 x
   2 bits (one 18 Kb BSRAM). Index pc[12:2], the same index as the L0,
   so BHT aliasing matches the L0's direct-mapped footprint. The read
   address register loads pc_d[12:2] with enable pc_en. These are the
   same D and enable the L0 already uses, so no new logic goes on the
   pc_d nets, only one more BSRAM address load per bit. Its output
   bht_a_q equals bht[pc_q[12:2]] as of the last PC load.
2. Copy B (override fetch): a second 2048 x 2 BSRAM written by the
   same training port. Its read address register loads
   redirect_target[12:2] with enable !ovr_q, exactly mirroring the
   existing ovr_tgt_q (same D, same enable). In an ovr_q cycle its
   output is therefore the counter for ovr_tgt_q, the address being
   fetched. Only low bits [12:2] are used: for JALR these come from
   the bottom of agu_sum's carry chain, and for branches from the flop
   alt_target. So copy B does not lengthen the redirect_target ->
   ovr_tgt_q path.
3. bht_ctr = ovr_pc_q ? bht_b_q : bht_a_q. The select is a flop and
   both data inputs are BSRAM outputs. This replaces fetch_pc ->
   LUTRAM -> 32:1 tree with one LUT after BSRAM clock-to-out. pt_imem
   and the L0-side pt keep their equations: they just read an early
   bht_ctr[1]. Prediction stays exact in override cycles (no static
   fallback).
4. Training stays as it is: bht_we/bht_widx/bht_wdata are EX flops,
   widened to an 11-bit index (pc[12:2]). They drive the write port of
   both copies directly. Read-during-write collisions (training write
   to the address being read on the same edge) may return a stale or
   undefined counter. This is safe because any 2-bit counter value
   only steers a prediction that EX verifies. There is no bad flag
   (unlike the L0, whose word must be correct). Initialise both copies
   to 2'b01 with a nested initial loop (Gowin caps one loop at 2000
   iterations; follow l0_icache.sv). Keep reset out of the RAM.
5. While the PC holds (pc_en = 0), copy A's output holds. While ovr_q
   holds, copy B's output holds. A training write that lands meanwhile
   is not seen until the next load. That is a performance-only
   staleness of a few cycles.

Net effect: the IF pt -> pc_d cone loses the fetch_pc mux plus the
RAM16 + MUX2_LUT5..8 tree (about 3-5 cells). The 32 LUTRAMs, their
write-enable decode and the u_ex -> u_if LUTRAM write path disappear.
Two BSRAMs are added (about 12 -> 14 of 46). No new term reaches EX,
ID, the redirect AND-OR, ovr_d, kill/stall or pc_d's select
structure. Cycles should stay within noise (expected 0 to -0.3%: the
2K table removes 512-entry aliasing, and per the trace, bimodal-1024
is already 39.6k vs 39.8k). Any gain is Fmax: IF's fetch_pc tier
drops out of the near-tie and the median is set by the EX
redirect -> ovr cone and the carry-select target path. Expect +1-3%
Fmax, and more if place_options 1/2 have the BHT cone at the top (the
critical path reported for r13s1 was s2_wb -> EX compare ->
ovr_l0_q).

Mandatory protocol: before deciding anything, write to
implementation_notes.md: cosim cycles
(`--bench --istall --dstall`), the 3-option median Fmax from
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`, each option's
Fmax and worst path, and the LUT/LUTRAM/BSRAM counts, for both the
champion and the change. Keep the change even if the median gain is
under the bar (it is formal-neutral and frees LUTs). Do not revert
silently. Run insn_beq_ch0 and pc_fwd_ch0 formal before submitting.

title: Store write-pending latch behind MEM: dmem port flops hold a not-ready store while the pipe advances
motivation:
Fresh all-options timing of the r13s1 champion (python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options,
run while writing this) shows place options 1/2 (the median, 100.874 MHz) with four cones tied
within 0.015 ns: (1) ID/EX sa_rf -> alu_a AND-OR -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result (15.208 ns, 6 cells),
(2) ID/EX s1_wb -> forward -> compare -> redirect -> ovr_q/ovr_l0_q/ovr_id_q/ovr_pc_q (15.206 ns,
9 cells), (3) pc_q -> BHT/pc_inc -> pc_d -> L0 BSRAM read address (15.206 ns, 11 cells),
(4) IF/ID instr[24] -> load-use compare -> backend_stall -> accept -> IF/ID CE (15.193 ns, 5 cells).
Option 0 (88.1 MHz) is an outlier with the same cones. LESSONS (r5s0, r10s0, r14s0) show that
cutting one or several cones of such a flat tier gains nothing, so the remaining lever is IPC
that adds no late term to any of the four cones.
The largest remaining cycle loss after the 2K BSRAM L0 is the dmem stall: every memory op in
EX/MEM freezes the whole pipe for ~0.28 expected cycles (22% not-ready, geometric). A store has
no result, so its stall is pure waste unless the next instruction needs the bus. LESSONS r11s0
says exactly how to retry this: "only as a write-pending latch behind MEM fed from EX/MEM flops,
leaving EX untouched" (r11s0 lost because it put port flops and lane logic on the EX AGU/forward
nets).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Let a store that meets !dmem_ready in MEM retire anyway and keep driving the bus from held
port flops, instead of freezing the pipeline.

1. mem_stage / ex_stage: split the dmem-port fields of EX/MEM (mem_addr, write_data, mem_width,
   port mem_write/mem_read bits) into a "port" group whose enable is
   !stall_ex_mem && !(port_wr_q && !dmem_ready) (port_wr_q = the port's own aligned-store bit;
   there is no separate pend flop: the port simply holds a store until the bus takes it, from its
   first MEM cycle on). Port ctrl bits are cleared by kill / div bubble like reg_q.ctrl. Their D inputs are unchanged (agu_sum, rs2, ctrl
   flops) so nothing new lands on the EX AGU/forward nets; only the flop enable (a flop-only
   signal) changes. io_dmemAddr stays a pure flop, so Gowin still absorbs it into the dmem BSRAM
   read-address register (a mux after the flop would break that absorption — do NOT add one).
   io_dmemWEn / io_dmemWData / io_dmemREn are computed from the port group as today.
2. A store in MEM no longer holds MEM/WB: it retires on its first MEM cycle whether or not the
   bus is ready. While port_wr_q && !dmem_ready, the store has already retired into MEM/WB (RVFI mem_* fields captured at that
   edge from the port group, so RVFI is unchanged), and the instructions behind it advance
   normally as long as they are not memory ops. The non-port EX/MEM fields keep advancing.
3. hazard_unit: dmem_stall becomes
     !dmem_ready && (ex_mem_mem_read                         // loads still wait, as today
                     || (port_wr_q && id_ex_mem_op && !ovr_ex)) // memop must not enter MEM
                                                                 // while the port holds a store
   where every input is a flop, so it stays an early side input of the redirect gating, the
   IF/ID accept and the EX/MEM / MEM/WB holds (no new level on cones 2 or 4). The !ovr_ex term
   preserves the existing invariant that no dmem stall occurs in an override cycle (flush_id
   relies on it). A store in EX/MEM never stalls any more: it writes (ready) or goes pending.
   A memop blocked behind a pending store is held in ID/EX exactly as a dmem stall holds it today
   (EX/MEM holds, MEM/WB valid cleared), so worst case equals the current behaviour.
4. Ordering/correctness: since memops cannot enter MEM while a store is pending, a later load can
   never read the old value, and the MMIO stop marker lands in program order. Liveness: the port
   clears on the next ready cycle, same fairness as today's stall.

Expected cycles: CoreMark ~2.9M instructions with ~10% stores -> ~80k store-stall cycles; the
store is followed by a non-memop in roughly 60-70% of cases (the pending write usually lands in
the next 1-2 cycles), so ~50-60k cycles saved (-1.5..-1.8%). Fmax: the only RTL touching the
four tied cones is a flop-only term merged into dmem_stall (port_wr_q, id_ex_mem_op,

title: Late-injected MUL: move the 33x33 DSP multiply from EX into MEM with a mul-use interlock
motivation:
The champion (r13s1, 100.874 MHz median, 3,442,936 cycles) has a flat
top tier in EX, and the 33x33 signed DSP multiply sits on it. Its operands
come from the forwarded alu_a/alu_b AND-OR, and its output passes the
mul_hi mux and the mul_sel result mux before the EX/MEM alu_result flop.
r14s0's post-change worst path was opb_val_18 -> alu_result_12, a MULH
product bit (b[18] can only reach p[44] = MULH bit 12), and r14s2's was
sb_wb -> alu_result_0. So "forward -> DSP -> mul mux -> result mux" is a
measured top-tier cone. Earlier micro-cuts on it (sign-gated extension
bits, syn_keep DSP operand copies) only moved fanout around and lost.
LESSONS r1s1 kept MUL single-cycle because a 1-cycle stall on every MUL
bought no Fmax on the 48 MHz core. That trade has now flipped. CoreMark
at 2K with 10 iterations runs only about 16k MULs out of 2.92M
instructions, mostly from matrix_mul_matrix and its bitextract variant
(N^3 = 729 each per iteration, N about 9). So even a bubble on every MUL
costs at most about 0.5% of cycles. A 1-2 LUT-level plus DSP-route cut
on a 9.9 ns tier is worth several times that.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Structural change at the EX/MEM stage boundary, in the style of
VexRiscv's MulPlugin: the multiplier result is injected one stage late.

1. EX (ex_stage.sv, alu.sv). Delete the multiplier from the ALU. Remove
   mul_p, mul_out and the `out = mul_sel ? mul_out : ...` level, so the
   ALU output is just nonmul | div_in. Register the multiplier operands
   into new EX/MEM fields:
     mul_a = {alu_a[31] & mul_a_signed, alu_a}
     mul_b = {alu_b[31] & mul_b_signed, alu_b}
   These are 33-bit flops taken from the existing alu_a/alu_b AND-ORs, so
   the DSP's 33 operand loads per forwarded bit become one flop load each.
   Also register mul_sel, mul_hi and the ALTOPS op into EX/MEM. Hold
   these fields on stall like the rest of EX/MEM. Give them no other
   consumer, so Gowin can absorb them into the DSP input registers
   (AREG/BREG).

2. MEM (mem_stage.sv). Compute mul_p = $signed(mul_a) * $signed(mul_b)
   from the EX/MEM flops and take mul_out = mul_hi ? p[63:32] : p[31:0].
   Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, use the same ALTOPS formulas as today, on
   the registered rs1/rs2 operands (keep the alu.sv and mem_stage.sv
   ALTOPS branches consistent with riscv-formal's insn_mul*.v). Fold
   mul_out into the existing wb_data select:
     mem_to_reg ? load : (mul_sel ? mul_out : alu_result)
   That select feeds MEM/WB.wb_data and the fwd_wb_q forward copy, so a
   MUL result reaches distance-2 consumers through the unchanged
   MEM/WB -> EX forward and the regfile write-first bypass.

3. Hazard (id_stage.sv, hazard_unit.sv, core.sv, core_pkg.sv). Add a
   control flop late_q to ID/EX, = v && (dec_mem_read || dec_is_mul),
   cleared by reset/flush exactly like mem_read_q. The hazard unit's
   load-use compare uses id_ex late_q in place of id_ex mem_read. That
   reuses the existing rd==rs1/rs2 comparator and adds no logic level:
   the same compare simply reads a different flop. A MUL followed
   immediately by a consumer then gets the same single bubble as a
   load. The consumer re-decodes the next cycle with the MUL in EX/MEM
   and picks the s?_wb select, so the EX/MEM.alu_result forward is never
   chosen for a MUL producer. mem_read keeps its own flop for the dmem
   port and the dstall term, so neither cone changes.

Nothing else moves. Branch/redirect, AGU, IF/L0, div_unit (still ORed
into nonmul), load path and RVFI wiring stay as they are. RVFI rd_wdata
is still MEM/WB.wb_data, and rs1/rs2_rdata still come from EX/MEM.rs?_val.

Expected effect. Cycles rise by at most the number of distance-1 MUL
consumers, about 16k, to roughly 3.46M (+0.5%). The EX alu_result cone
loses the DSP, the hi/lo mux and the mul_sel mux. The alu_a/alu_b nets
lose their DSP fanout, which also lightens the redirect/AGU cones that
share the forward AND-OR region. The new MEM cone (DSP input reg ->
33x33 product -> 2 LUT -> wb flops) starts at a flop with no forward mux
in front, about 1.5-2 ns shorter than today's EX version. If Fmax rises
from 100.9 to 106-108 MHz, fitness is about 307-313 (+5 to +7%).

title: Predict every fetch from the BSRAM fetch-cache entry (not the imem word), taking the imem predecode/carry-select adder off pc_d, and use the freed next-PC slot for an ID-updated return stack verified through EX's existing cmp_eq arm
motivation:
On r13s1 (292.99, 100.874 MHz median, seeds [88.1, 100.9, 100.9], 3,442,936
cycles) the predictor's IPC headroom is only ~3% of cycles (~53.5k branch
mispredicts + JALRs at 2 cycles each), so a predictor change has to make the
IF next-PC cone shorter, not just add accuracy. Today pc_d (which feeds pc_q
and the L0 BSRAM read-address register) is
imem_ready ? (pt_imem ? tgt_imem : pc_inc) : (pt_l0 ? l0_tgt : pc_inc), and
its imem arm is the deepest IF cone: imem BSRAM out -> BRANCH/JAL predecode +
imm1 -> imm_lo -> 19-bit fetch_pc + imm add -> {sign, carry} hi select -> pt
mux -> pc_d (r12s0/r13s2's worst paths were in this IF region, ovr_tgt_q ->
... -> alt_target at 25 cells). Since r13s1, the 2K-entry BSRAM L0 holds the
same word plus its fill-time target (tgt) and predecode bits (jal_ok,
br_ok) for all hot code, with data ready at the start of the fetch cycle.
So the imem-side predictor is redundant whenever the L0 hits, which after
warm-up is almost always. r12s2 says to revisit returns only after a cut
gives the IF next-PC cone real slack. This hypothesis is that cut, with
the return stack on top of it.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Part A (the cut). Predict only from the L0 entry, whether or not imem is
ready: pt = l0_hit_pred && (l0_jal_ok || (l0_br_ok && bht_ctr[1]) || l0_ret_ok),
ptgt = l0 target (or the RAS top for a ret, part B),
pc_d = pt ? ptgt : pc_inc. The imem predecode and carry-select adder stay
only on the fill path (the staged fill flops, already off pc_d) and on the
IF/ID alt_target D (which still needs pc+imm for a not-taken prediction;
alt_target D = pt ? pc_inc : (imem_ready ? tgt_imem : l0_tgt), the same mux
as today, ending at a flop, not at pc_d / the BSRAM address).
imem_ready leaves the pt and pc_d selects; it still selects the IF/ID word.
l0_hit_pred is the existing hit (valid, tag, in_range, !bad), and !ovr_l0_q
as today (no L0 lookup in override cycles, so a redirect target is never
predicted; that costs ~0.2% cycles). If the hit compare is too deep for the
pt select, precompute in_range as a flop next to the PC and keep `bad`
flop-derived. Correctness rule: a word fetched on an L0 miss is predicted
not-taken. A not-taken aligned JAL must then redirect in EX. Do this
without a new redirect term: in ID, a valid aligned JAL with pred=0 sets
BOTH sel_eq and sel_ne (so redirect = cmp_eq || !cmp_eq = 1), and its
alt_target is pc+imm (tgt_imem from the imem arm). A predicted aligned
JAL keeps all selects 0, as today. Misaligned JAL/BRANCH are never
predicted and keep selects 0 (trap, no redirect).
Part B (return stack, only after A holds the 3-option median). Add one
fill-time predecode bit ret_ok (word == 32'h00008067, `jalr x0, 0(ra)`)
to the L0 entry. The entry goes from 67 to 68 bits, which still fits the
same 8 x (2048x9) BSRAMs. Keep a 4- or 8-entry RAS: LUTRAM with a flop
pointer, or flops. IF only READS ras_top (an async read off the flop
pointer, so early) as the third pc_d source on the l0 side:
pc_d = AND-OR of {l0_tgt: hit&&(jal_ok||br_ok&&ctr)}, {ras_top: hit&&ret_ok},
{pc_inc: otherwise}. That is no wider than today's imem_ready/pt 2x2 mux.
All RAS UPDATES come from IF/ID flops in ID, never from pc_en, accept or the
imem predecode: a one-shot ifid_new_q flop (IF/ID captured a fetched word on
the last edge) && !ovr_id. Push pc+4 (IF/ID.pc + 4, a short incrementer
from flops) when ID decodes JAL/JALR with rd = x1/x5. Pop when ID holds a
ret that was predicted (pred_taken). Wrong-path updates only cost accuracy.
Carry the RAS top read at fetch into IF/ID (ret_tgt flop). Verify in EX
with no new redirect input: ID ORs ret_tgt into the ID/EX.rs2_val D of a
predicted ret (its rs2 field is x0, so s2_rf=1 and rs2 = rs2_val), and sets
sel_ne, so EX redirects iff rs1 != predicted target. The JALR term becomes
jalr_unpred_q && !agu1, where jalr_unpred_q is a flop replacing is_jalr.
A predicted ret whose target is misaligned (agu1) traps. It must redirect
to pc+4, so make the redirect_target select
(is_jalr && !agu1) ? agu_sum : alt_target, with alt_target = pc+4 for a
predicted ret. agu1 comes from 2 forwarded bits, so the select stays far
ahead of the agu_sum carry. Mask the RVFI rs2_rdata of a predicted ret
back to 0. That path is RVFI-only and pruned. Returns cost 2 cycles today
(13.7k returns -> ~27k cycles, ~0.8%).
Expected: part A is IPC-neutral to -0.3% (only cold L0 misses and
override-cycle targets lose prediction) and takes the deepest IF
arithmetic off pc_d and the L0 address register, worth 0-4% Fmax if the
IF cone is in the median options' top tier. Part B is +0.6-0.8% cycles at
no pc_d cost. Mandatory protocol, carried over from the null results of
r11s2/r14s1: (1) build A, run cosim (--bench --istall --dstall) and write
the cycle count to implementation_notes.md, then run
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` and write all three Fmax
values and the median's worst path BEFORE deciding anything. (2) Add B, and
write the same numbers again. (3) Keep B only if the median does not fall.
Revert A only if it drops the median below 100.874, and record that in the
notes.
